sections.section_path: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > “Bad split” deep diagnostics > B) Policy precedence causing unexpected routing
sections.heading: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > “Bad split” deep diagnostics > B) Policy precedence causing unexpected routing
sections.content:
B) Policy precedence causing unexpected routing

**Checks:**

- Fallback routing policy may override canary selection.
- Region routing constraints may redirect canary traffic to baseline in some regions.
- Quota/rate limiting policy may shed canary disproportionately.

**Mitigation:**

- Prefer rollback if behavior is not easily explained.
- Escalate to Policy Engine if denies/overrides suspected.

---

sections.section_path: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Diagnostic procedure > Step 1 — Confirm truth: what is configured vs what is observed
sections.heading: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Diagnostic procedure > Step 1 — Confirm truth: what is configured vs what is observed
sections.content:
Diagnostic procedure

Step 1 — Confirm truth: what is configured vs what is observed

1) **Fetch rollout details** (source of truth = orchestrator):

   - Verify state: DRAFT / RUNNING / PAUSED / ROLLED_BACK / COMPLETED
   - Verify current step target percentage
   - Verify region scope and any partial-apply warnings

2) **Compare to observed traffic**:

   - Look at request counts per cohort over the last 10–15 minutes.
   - Compare overall and per region.

**Interpretation tips:**

- At low volumes, small absolute differences look like large % differences; check confidence intervals and absolute counts.
- Deterministic cohorting can produce slight variance at very low traffic; treat >2–3x deviation (or persistent deviation >15 minutes) as suspicious.

sections.section_path: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Where to look (dashboards/logs)
sections.heading: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Where to look (dashboards/logs)
sections.content:
Where to look (dashboards/logs)

> Replace placeholders with tenant/route/rollout identifiers.

sections.section_path: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Customer communication guidance (Support + Oncall)
sections.heading: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Customer communication guidance (Support + Oncall)
sections.content:
Customer communication guidance (Support + Oncall)

- If customer impact is active: inform Support that rollout has been paused/rolled back and provide ETA for follow-up.
- Avoid blaming “metrics are wrong”; instead say “cohort measurements are being verified” and that rollout safety has been prioritized.
- Provide a short audit-friendly reason for rollback/pause in the incident ticket.

---

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Dedupe key
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Dedupe key
sections.content:
Dedupe key

Incident-bot dedupes based on:

- model_id + model_version + runtime_build_id + kernel_set_id + hardware_sku (+ region if present) + metric_type + severity

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Appendix A: Example Per-Model Overrides (illustrative)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Appendix A: Example Per-Model Overrides (illustrative)
sections.content:
Appendix A: Example Per-Model Overrides (illustrative)

- Top model (customer-critical): paging at +15% p95 E2E, -12% tokens/sec, stricter min token count.
- High-variance model: warning only, wider thresholds (+15% / -10%), region-specific baseline enabled.
- New kernel rollout candidate: temporary tighter warning (+8%) during rollout ring, but paging remains at default until validated.

sections.section_path: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Severity guidance (SRE)
sections.heading: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Severity guidance (SRE)
sections.content:
Severity guidance (SRE)

Use the following guidelines when declaring severity:

- **SEV-1:** Widespread routing impact (many tenants), large latency/5xx increase, or rollout control plane causing sustained customer outage.
- **SEV-2:** Single large tenant impacted (SLA risk), or split mismatch causing repeated auto-pauses/rollbacks with user-visible degradation.
- **SEV-3:** Rollout stuck without service impact (customer blocked but production stable) or split mismatch limited to one region with low traffic.

If in doubt and customer-facing impact is ongoing, escalate severity early; mitigation (freeze/rollback) is typically low-risk.

---

sections.section_path: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Escalation paths > Component-specific escalation
sections.heading: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > Escalation paths > Component-specific escalation
sections.content:
Component-specific escalation

- **Smart Routing / Data plane split enforcement:** Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon (routing oncall)
- **Telemetry / cohort tagging & aggregation:** Logan Wright / Caleb Johnson
- **Policy engine / guardrails / approvals:** Jordan Lee / Benji Okafor
- **Security / audit logging integrity:** Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Alternatives Considered > C) Per-region baselines always on
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Alternatives Considered > C) Per-region baselines always on
sections.content:
C) Per-region baselines always on

Pros:

- Reduces false positives due to cross-region fleet differences.

Cons:

- Baseline explosion (more artifacts and config), operational overhead.

Decision: Region is optional and only enabled for models/regions where observed variance requires it.

sections.section_path: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > “Rollout stuck” deep diagnostics > A) Stuck in metric evaluation
sections.heading: Runbook Rollout Stuck Or Bad Split > “Rollout stuck” deep diagnostics > A) Stuck in metric evaluation
sections.content:
“Rollout stuck” deep diagnostics

A) Stuck in metric evaluation

**Checks:**

- Telemetry ingestion delay (pipeline lag)
- Metric evaluation timeouts in orchestrator logs
- Missing cohort tags

**Mitigation:**

- Pause rollout.
- If health regression: rollback.
- If only evaluation stuck but traffic split correct: keep paused and escalate to Telemetry + Orchestrator.

Shiproom Runner Personal Prep Log

Source type: google_drive
Document ID: dsid_5fc2dba9f6ac4af2b49b4f546a4298d0
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Shiproom runner: personal prep log and sticky notes

Purpose: quick, scannable personal notes for running the shiproom and weekly readiness sync. Organized as prep items, live-run cues, and follow-up actions. Not a polished playbook — my sticky running list + prompts to escalate.

DAY-BEFORE / 24-48H CHECKS (quick hits)

- Validate Dedicated pool health dashboard (console > Dedicated > Pool-5). Look for 90th pct latency spike > 20% vs baseline. If spike: page SRE and tag 'pool-5'.
- Confirm model pin assignments for weekend rollouts: model = rwx-v2-quant, pinned to image-2026-02-28. Cross-check with model-catalog ticket.
- Ensure canary capacity reserved: 3 instances w/ low-priority burst. If not reserved, open ticket to infra (email infra-runbooks).
- Verify last smoke-run results (smoke/last-run.json) — critical checks: health endpoints, prefix caching, stream stability. Mark any failing check with TODO.

MEETING AGENDA (for my 10–15 min run)
1) Quick status (30s each): Hosted API, Dedicated, Private — 3 bullet lines max.
2) Go/No-Go candidate items (3) — call out owner for decision.
3) High-risk regressions & mitigations (A/B, rollbacks, fallback).
4) Open action items from last week (owners + ETA).
5) Escalations and customer-impacting items.
GO/NO-GO CHECKLIST (my shorthand)

- Safety: latest canary passed golden prompt set? [yes/no] — if no -> NO-GO and block rollout. Owner: Priya.
- Latency: 95th <= SLO (hosted) and Dedicated 90th within committed window? [ok/warn/fail] Owner: Jordan.
- Throughput: capacity test at target qps for model variant (rwx-v2-quant) >= 90% predicted. Owner: Marco (perf eng).
- Telemetry: traces + logs flowing to observability (no gaps > 5 min). Owner: Observability on-call.
- Rollback plan: image rollback verified in staging (time-to-recover < 10m). Owner: me (Aisha) — pre-check: rehearse command set.

LIVE-RUN CUES (during shiproom)

- If latency alert fires: call out metric, ask SRE to confirm impact (hosted vs dedicated). If impact is hosted only -> consider global throttles, otherwise trigger capacity burst.
- If canary fails: pause rollout, gather failing prompts, escalate to Applied ML for quality triage. Capture failing prompt examples in the meeting notes.
- If control plane flaps: deploy cross-region fallback policy, set communication to CS + site-status.

SMOKE-TEST QUICK-LOOK (ordered)
1) /health (all regions) — expect 200 and healthy=true.
2) golden prompt generation (3 variants) — check for coherent output and stable token length.
3) streaming socket smoke (5 simulated clients) — no connection resets.
4) KV cache hit-rate sanity check (> 30% for typical workloads).
5) auth flow: token validation for dev key and prod key.
RISKS I CARE ABOUT (notes to self)

- Quantized model edge cases: hallucinations on long-context prompts unseen in evals. Watch for uptick in hallucination rate on live eval monitors.
- Autoscale cold starts: small percentage of cold starts can push P95 over threshold. Keep warmup policy on for first 2h post-deploy.
- Third-party infra patch windows (cloud provider) could impact Dedicated zones — pre-check weekly maintenance calendar.

OPEN ACTIONS (make sure to call out in meeting)

sections.section_path: Shiproom Runner Personal Prep Log
sections.heading: Shiproom Runner Personal Prep Log
sections.content:
- A1: Priya — re-run golden prompt suite with latest model (due 2026-03-03). Status: running.
- A2: Jordan — validate Dedicated pool latency anomaly root cause, post short RCA (due 2026-03-05). Status: investigating.
- A3: Marco — confirm scaling headroom numbers for expected QPS spike; provide conservative headroom estimate (due 2026-03-04).
- A4: Aisha (me) — rehearse rollback commands in staging and record exact steps in private playbook (due 2026-03-02).
- A5: Eng-sre on-call — add trace tag for canary requests to make debugging faster (due 2026-03-03).

NOTES-TO-SELF / RUN-TIME SNIPPETS

- Keep the Launch Channel pinned and set ephemeral notifications: only @here for major go/no-go decisions.
- One-sentence status template for quick updates: "Area — short-state (ok/warn/fail) — top-1 mitigation if warn/fail". Use this when I call status.
- If we need to delay: propose a 1-hour cool-down + redo canary after fixes.

ESCALATION CONTACTS (quick)

- SRE on-call (pager): pager.sre@redwood.internal — send with subject: "shiproom: [area] [short tag]"
- Applied ML: priya.nair@redwood.com (for model-quality escalations)
- Infra runbook slack: #infra-runbooks (use slash /runbook deploy-rollback)

POST-MEETING FOLLOW-UP FORMAT (what I send to channel)

- TL;DR (1 line)
- Decisions (go/no-go + what changed)
- Owners + actions (one-line per action with ETA)
- Customer-facing items (any comms to CS + suggested text)

EXAMPLE QUICK COMMS (copyable)

- "TL;DR: Go for staged rollout (canary ok). Action: Priya to finish regression suite; Jordan to monitor Dedicated P95. Aisha to coordinate rollback rehearsal."
- "Customer note (for CS): We observed intermittent latency in Dedicated pool during preflight; mitigation is increased warmup and a temporary capacity bump. ETA for final fix: 48h."

MY PERSONAL CHECKLIST BEFORE HAND-OFF

- Confirm notes & action items added to central release tracker (JIRA-RELEASE-2026).
- Make sure ownership is explicit (no ambiguous "eng team" lines).
- Leave a 15-min buffer after the meeting for async follow-ups and handover to ops.

FRAGMENTS / THINGS I WANT TO INVESTIGATE (later)

- Can we automate the canary prompt selection so it's representative of top-100 queries? (pitch to applied-ml)
- Metric to add: per-model hallucination delta vs baseline (daily) — needs logging hook.
- Explore a one-click rollback UI in console for small teams (longer-term product ask).

END-OF-DAY LOG (fill after shiproom)

- Outcome: [GO / NO-GO] — notes: _____
- Actions I triggered: list with timestamps
- Follow-ups I delegated: list with owner + ETA

(Misc scratch lines)

- remember: breathe. keep the meeting short. if debate > 3min, move to async deep-dive.

-- Aisha

sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Root cause > RC3: Alert policy mismatch with evaluator grouping (contributing)
sections.content:
RC3: Alert policy mismatch with evaluator grouping (contributing)

The alert rules aggregated time series on a different dimension set than the evaluator used for baseline comparison.

- The evaluator grouped by (model, model_version, region, hardware_sku, runtime_build).
- Warning alert queries grouped by (model, region) for readability.
- Paging rules grouped by (model) only for top-model simplicity.

This mismatch made it possible for a small, noisy slice (e.g., one SKU) to trigger evaluator regressions while alerts appeared “global”, causing confusion in triage.

sections.section_path: Pr 867001 Introduce Token Stage Cohorting And Route Matrix Alerting
sections.heading: Pr 867001 Introduce Token Stage Cohorting And Route Matrix Alerting
sections.content:
Pr 867001 Introduce Token Stage Cohorting And Route Matrix Alerting

Source type: github
Document ID: dsid_c1a6a71323c04c1ba5445aadea340362
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
introduce-token-stage-cohorting-and-route-matrix-alerting

Context: long-tail token cost and multi-stage latency spikes frequently surface only when a request traverses several model-serving stages (tokenization, encoder, decode, fallback). Existing alerts were per-route and per-quantile but lacked a compact way to group requests by 'stage footprint' and automatically route alerting weight to the stage(s) most likely responsible. Motivation: reduce alert noise and accelerate RCA by grouping invocations into stage-aware cohorts and deriving a route x stage alert matrix that attributes SLO violations to the most likely pipeline stage. What this PR does: 1) Adds a lightweight token_stage_cohort service that computes a deterministic cohort key per invocation based on stage-level metrics (token counts per stage, kv-cache hit pattern, decode-batch size) and stores short-lived cohort aggregates. 2) Introduces an alert route-matrix generator that consumes cohort rollups and emits alert bindings which bias escalation to the top-k stages for that route. 3) Adds a new dashboard focused on cohort drift, stage heatmaps, and per-cohort cost/latency breakdown to help oncall quickly validate root cause hypotheses. 4) Wires the generator into the existing alerting pipeline with a safe canary rollout and automatic quiet-window attenuation to avoid regressing noise. Compatibility and rollout: service defaults to read-only mode until flagged by a feature flag; alert generation starts cross-account in a low-sensitivity mode (only P90/P99) and is then ramped after 72h of monitoring. Testing: unit and integration tests added; ran a 48h synthetic replay against production-like traces (see test run in CI). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Dashboard panels - [x] Docs for oncall and runbook - [x] Feature-flagged rollout Plan for operators: deploy to staging -> enable feature flag -> monitor cohort drift and false-positive rate -> bump sensitivity -> full rollout. Links: Linear ENG-1248 (cohorting design) and PM-432 (dashboard spec).
Diego: Can cohort keys be stable across model version rollouts? Added suggestion to include model-version hash in key derivation. Response: we now namespace cohort keys with model-major-version and include fallback mapping in cohort_store.proto.
Priya: Alert noise risk—please limit initial sensitivity and provide quiet-window behavior. Response: implemented quiet-window attenuation and low-sensitivity defaults; documented in docs/observability/token-cohorting.md.
Liam: test coverage looks good but add an e2e replay with partial KV-cache misses. Response: added synthetic KV miss replay in tests/integration/test_cohorting_flow.py and CI run shows stable results.

sections.content:
Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm

Source type: confluence
Document ID: dsid_58bdb9f3bb4241e089f4f2b102765db4
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Postmortem: Perf Canary False-Positive Alert Storm (baseline drift + cardinality)

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Summary
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Summary
sections.content:
Summary

On 2026-02-12, the production performance canary generated a burst of false-positive alerts across multiple models and regions shortly after enabling warning + paging rules in the first expansion beyond the initial 2-model rollout. Alerts were high volume (warning + paging) and repeatedly reopened due to dedupe failures, resulting in on-call interruption and a temporary release freeze request.

There was **no confirmed customer-facing latency regression** attributable to this incident. The event was an alerting/observability failure caused primarily by (1) **baseline drift + baseline key mismatch** and (2) **metric label cardinality inflation** that fragmented the canary’s time series, defeating min-sample gating and dedupe.

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Impact > Customer impact
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Impact > Customer impact
sections.content:
Impact

Customer impact

- **None confirmed.** Runtime and customer SLO dashboards did not show correlated sustained p95 latency increases for customer traffic.

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Impact > Internal impact
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Impact > Internal impact
sections.content:
Internal impact

- **Paging noise:** 19 paging alerts over ~38 minutes (with multiple re-pages due to missing dedupe keys).
- **Warning noise:** 60+ warning alerts over ~75 minutes.
- **Operational disruption:** SRE on-call and runtime on-call diverted to triage; release engineering requested a short freeze while signals stabilized.
- **Confidence impact:** Reduced trust in the perf canary as a rollout gate until remediations were in place.

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Resolution and immediate mitigations
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Resolution and immediate mitigations
sections.content:
Resolution and immediate mitigations

Actions taken during the incident:

1. **Disabled paging rules** for perf-canary regressions (kept warning-level visibility). (Owner: SRE on-call)
2. **Rolled back canary model coverage** to the previously stable 3-model configuration. (Owner: Runtime on-call)
3. **Pinned evaluator to fixed baseline artifacts** (no rolling updates) until schema/keys were corrected. (Owner: Nadia Rahman)
4. **Hotfix to drop high-cardinality labels** from canary metrics (`workload_run_id`, `prompt_template_id`, full `route`). (Owner: Logan Wright)

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Appendix > Key decision: baseline missing is a health signal
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Appendix > Key decision: baseline missing is a health signal
sections.content:
Appendix

Key decision: baseline missing is a health signal

We changed behavior from:

- “baseline missing → compare against default thresholds (often too strict)”

to:

- “baseline missing → emit canary health warning + stop regression evaluation for that grouping until baseline exists”.

Rationale: baseline absence is an operational/config issue. Treating it as a performance regression creates noisy pages and reduces trust.

- Runbook: Responding to perf canary regression alerts: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-perf-regression-canary-alert.json
- Dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/perf-canary-dashboards-spec.json

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Lessons learned > What didn’t go well
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Lessons learned > What didn’t go well
sections.content:
What didn’t go well

- Baseline missing → fallback thresholds created a failure mode where instrumentation/config drift looked like performance regressions.
- Cardinality review was incomplete; labels that seemed “harmless” for logs caused large fragmentation for metrics.
- Alert grouping mismatch created confusion (alerts appeared “global” while underlying series were per-SKU/per-region slices).
- Dedupe failures amplified the incident by creating parallel incident-bot threads and repeated pages.

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Lessons learned > What went well
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Lessons learned > What went well
sections.content:
Lessons learned

What went well

- On-call validated against independent customer-traffic dashboards quickly and avoided an unnecessary rollback of the runtime.
- Teams (Runtime/SRE/Telemetry) coordinated rapidly; paging rules were disabled within ~20 minutes.
- The canary’s strict “no customer prompts” policy kept investigation clean (no privacy concerns during deep dive).

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Root cause > RC1: Baseline drift + key mismatch (primary)
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Root cause > RC1: Baseline drift + key mismatch (primary)
sections.content:
Root cause

RC1: Baseline drift + key mismatch (primary)

Baselines were stored per (model, runtime_version, hardware_sku, region) in the baseline store, but the canary emitted/evaluated metrics with an expanded set of labels including transient fields and “bucketed” dimensions that were not part of the baseline artifact key.

Specifically:

- The canary evaluation path constructed a baseline key using **(model, model_version, runtime_build, region, hardware_sku, prompt_shape_bucket)**.
- Baseline artifacts were generated for **(model, model_version, runtime_build, region, hardware_sku)** only (no prompt bucket), and in some cases had **region omitted** (older artifacts) because early staging used a simplified schema.
- When the lookup did not match, the evaluator fell back to default thresholds, which are intentionally conservative and therefore easier to breach.

Additionally, baseline updates were set to a rolling policy during the first expansion.

- A rolling baseline can be valid, but in this case it introduced “baseline drift” during a period of changing model coverage and metric schema. Drift made alerts oscillate because the baseline distribution was not stable across the same label set.

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Lessons learned > Where we got lucky
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Lessons learned > Where we got lucky
sections.content:
Where we got lucky

- The storm happened during an expansion window and not during a high-risk runtime rollout; impact was primarily internal.

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Root cause > RC2: Metric label cardinality inflation (primary)
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Root cause > RC2: Metric label cardinality inflation (primary)
sections.content:
RC2: Metric label cardinality inflation (primary)

Several labels unintentionally increased cardinality:

- `prompt_template_id` (seeded but still high cardinality across the prompt set)
- `workload_run_id` (unique per canary run)
- `route` (included full internal route string with version suffix)

This caused:

- Fragmentation of histograms/counters into many short-lived series.
- “Min samples” checks passing on one series while the alert query aggregated differently.
- Increased ingestion lag and higher query variance due to sparse buckets.

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Corrective and preventative actions (CPAs) > Implemented (completed)
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Corrective and preventative actions (CPAs) > Implemented (completed)
sections.content:
Corrective and preventative actions (CPAs)

Implemented (completed)

- **Baseline key normalization:** Baseline lookup now uses a canonical key:
  - `model_id` (canonical registry ID)
  - `model_version` (registry version)
  - `runtime_build_id`
  - `hardware_sku`
  - `region`
  - (explicitly does *not* include prompt bucket or run IDs)
- **Metric label contract:** Reduced emitted labels to an approved set; added a CI check that fails if new labels are added without review.
- **Evaluator “baseline missing” behavior:** Baseline missing is now treated as **“canary unhealthy”** (warn once) rather than “assume default regression thresholds”.
- **Min-sample + dampening alignment:** Alert rules now match the evaluator grouping and require:
  - minimum N requests per grouping
  - sustained breach across multiple evaluation intervals
- **Incident-bot dedupe key update:** Dedupe keys now include (model_id, model_version, region, hardware_sku, runtime_build_id, alert_type).

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Follow-up validation plan
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Follow-up validation plan
sections.content:
Follow-up validation plan

Before re-enabling paging and using signals as rollout gates, we will:

1. Run a **7-day warning-only bake** with expanded coverage and confirm:
   - baseline hit-rate > 99.5%
   - no unexpected label growth (cardinality budget)
   - alert volume within noise budget
2. Re-enable paging for **one top model** in one region with clear success criteria.
3. Only after stable paging, enable rollout gate consumption in “advisory” mode for 2 weeks, then move to “blocking” mode.

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > What happened (symptoms)
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > What happened (symptoms)
sections.content:
What happened (symptoms)

The canary’s regression evaluator compared observed p95 latency/tokens-sec against per-model baselines. After model expansion:

- Many evaluations used **fallback baseline values** because the baseline lookup key did not match (baseline existed under a different dimension set).
- Metric series were fragmented by high-cardinality labels; the regression evaluator saw many “small-N” series and oscillated between “enough samples” and “not enough samples” depending on which series was queried.
- Alert rules did not consistently enforce **minimum sample size across the same grouping** used by the evaluator, which allowed small, noisy slices to trip thresholds.
- incident-bot dedupe keys lacked stable identifiers for (model, version, region, sku, runtime_build), so the same underlying symptom created repeated threads/pages.

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Corrective and preventative actions (CPAs) > Planned (in progress)
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Corrective and preventative actions (CPAs) > Planned (in progress)
sections.content:
Planned (in progress)

- **Region/SKU-aware thresholds:** Allow thresholds that differ by SKU/region where variance is known to differ (documented + versioned).
- **Baseline drift guardrails:** Rolling baselines require an explicit “baseline update window” and block updates during rollout expansion or telemetry schema changes.
- **Canary alert gating:** Rollout gates will consume only “high-confidence” regression signals (enforced min samples + stable baseline + low ingestion lag).

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Detection
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Detection
sections.content:
Detection

- Detected via automated paging to the on-call channel and incident-bot threads.
- Secondary signal: Grafana dashboard showed many “regression detected” annotations without corresponding customer latency change.

sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Timeline (UTC)

sections.section_path: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Contributing factors
sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Contributing factors
sections.content:
Contributing factors

- **Schema change during rollout:** Metric label set changed between the initial 3-model rollout and expansion.
- **Baseline artifact heterogeneity:** Some baseline artifacts were generated in a prod-like shadow environment with a different region/SKU mapping.
- **Telemetry ingestion delay:** During the event, ingestion lag fluctuated (minutes), causing “sawtooth” alert evaluation.
- **Runbook ambiguity:** The runbook guided “compare to baseline” but didn’t explicitly call out “baseline not found → fallback thresholds” as a first-class failure mode.

sections.heading: Postmortem Perf Canary False Positive Alert Storm > Impact > Services/systems involved
sections.content:

- incident-bot alert handler

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Summary
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Summary
sections.content:
Summary

This ADR defines how the production performance canary computes baselines and evaluates regressions for per-model serving performance (primarily p95 latency and tokens/sec). It documents:

- Baseline computation approach (rolling vs fixed) and when each is used.
- Regression thresholds (warning vs paging) and how they are applied.
- Minimum sample sizes and confidence requirements to avoid noisy alerts.
- Anti-flap / dedupe logic to prevent alert storms during drift, telemetry delays, or small-sample variance.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Decision Drivers
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Decision Drivers
sections.content:
Decision Drivers

1. **Low noise / high trust**: warnings should be useful; pages should be rare and high-confidence.
2. **Fast detection**: detect regressions within ~10–30 minutes for top models in covered regions.
3. **Attribution**: baseline keys must align to dimensions needed for root cause (runtime build, kernel tags, SKU).
4. **Operational simplicity**: SRE/on-call should have a predictable interpretation of “regression vs baseline,” including during ongoing rollouts.
5. **Guardrails against drift and telemetry issues**: avoid alert storms caused by baseline drift, delayed metric ingestion, and label cardinality errors.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Implementation Notes / Requirements
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Implementation Notes / Requirements
sections.content:
Implementation Notes / Requirements

1. Baseline artifacts must be stored in an access-controlled, versioned store with auditability (who/when created).
2. Canary config must support per-model overrides:
   - thresholds by severity
   - whether region-specific keys are enabled
   - “top model” flag affecting paging eligibility
3. Alert payloads must include:
   - observed value, baseline value, percent change
   - sample counts and token counts
   - runtime_build_id, kernel_set_id, hardware_sku, region
   - links to dashboards, traces, and runbook
4. Changes to default thresholds must go through an ADR update or SRE-approved change request.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Status
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Status
sections.content:
Status

Published.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Context / Problem
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Context / Problem
sections.content:
Context / Problem

Redwood’s serving runtime changes frequently (kernel selection updates, scheduler heuristics, model config changes, GPU fleet changes, and staged rollouts). We need an always-on canary that:

- Detects real p95 latency regressions and throughput drops early.
- Produces actionable signals for attribution (kernel vs scheduler vs infra).
- Avoids paging on expected variance and baseline drift (e.g., slow fleet mix changes or regional differences).

The key design tension is baseline choice:

- A **fixed baseline** is stable and easy to reason about during rollouts, but can become stale as hardware/driver stacks and workloads evolve.
- A **rolling baseline** adapts over time, but can drift (masking regressions) or create false positives if drift is misinterpreted as regression.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds
sections.content:
Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds

Source type: confluence
Document ID: dsid_a3f94972391244f38ef773c05926af83
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
ADR-0142: Perf Canary Baselines, Regression Thresholds, Min Sample Sizes, and Anti-Flap Logic

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Baseline Keys (What defines “like-for-like”)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Baseline Keys (What defines “like-for-like”)
sections.content:
Baseline Keys (What defines “like-for-like”)

Baseline artifacts and regression evaluation are keyed by the following dimensions:

**Required baseline key fields (v1):**

- model_id (canonical model identifier)
- model_version (registry version / hash)
- runtime_build_id (serving runtime build tag)
- kernel_set_id (kernel selection/version identifier)
- hardware_sku (e.g., H100-80GB, A100-80GB)

**Optional fields (only when variance requires it):**

- region (enabled for regions with materially different fleet/network characteristics)
- capacity_tier (hosted vs dedicated pools) when pools differ materially

Notes:

- We do NOT key baselines by customer, endpoint, or prompt content (privacy + cardinality constraints).
- Scheduler configuration flags that materially change behavior must be reflected either in runtime_build_id or an explicit scheduler_profile tag (introduced only if needed; kept off by default to control cardinality).

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Regression Definition > Core comparison method (v1)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Regression Definition > Core comparison method (v1)
sections.content:
Core comparison method (v1)

For each metric M and key K in each evaluation window W:

- Compute observed metric value O(K, W).
- Fetch baseline value B(K) and baseline variability estimates when available.
- Compute percent change: Δ = (O - B) / B.

We use percent change thresholds with guardrails (min samples + sustained breach). Percent thresholds are chosen because:

- Different models have different absolute latencies.
- p95 is the primary SLO-relevant tail metric.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Baseline Computation > Rolling health baseline (calibration only)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Baseline Computation > Rolling health baseline (calibration only)
sections.content:
Rolling health baseline (calibration only)

- Window: trailing 7 days, excluding periods marked as “rollout” or “incident.”
- Aggregation: daily aggregates with robust statistics (median-of-daily-p95) to reduce sensitivity to short spikes.
- Purpose:
  - detect slow drift (e.g., fleet changes) that may warrant generating a new fixed baseline
  - suggest region/SKU overrides when variance is consistently higher

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Alternatives Considered > A) Pure rolling baseline (always updated)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Alternatives Considered > A) Pure rolling baseline (always updated)
sections.content:
Alternatives Considered

A) Pure rolling baseline (always updated)

Pros:

- Adapts to drift without explicit re-baselining.

Cons:

- Risk of masking slow regressions (baseline chases the regression).
- Hard to use for rollout gating (“moving goalposts”).
- Susceptible to alert storms if rolling logic is impacted by label bugs or ingestion gaps.

Decision: Rejected for paging/gating. Allowed only as a secondary calibration signal.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Appendix A: Example Per-Model Overrides (illustrative)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Appendix A: Example Per-Model Overrides (illustrative)
sections.content:
Appendix A: Example Per-Model Overrides (illustrative)

- Top model (customer-critical): paging at +15% p95 E2E, -12% tokens/sec, stricter min token count.
- High-variance model: warning only, wider thresholds (+15% / -10%), region-specific baseline enabled.
- New kernel rollout candidate: temporary tighter warning (+8%) during rollout ring, but paging remains at default until validated.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Metrics Covered
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Metrics Covered
sections.content:
Metrics Covered

Baselines and regressions are computed for:

- End-to-end latency: p50, p95, p99 (ms)
- Runtime-only latency: p50, p95, p99 (ms) (excludes network/client)
- Prefill latency and decode latency (ms)
- Queueing time (ms) (scheduler-level)
- Tokens/sec (overall, and decode tokens/sec where available)
- Batch size distribution (for attribution)
- KV cache hit rate (where applicable; informational at v1)

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Open Questions (tracked outside ADR)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Open Questions (tracked outside ADR)
sections.content:
Open Questions (tracked outside ADR)

- Whether to introduce a scheduler_profile tag in baseline keys (cardinality vs attribution benefit).
- Whether to page on runtime-only p95 for certain enterprise-dedicated pools (when E2E has additional network variance).
- Whether to incorporate a lightweight statistical test (e.g., bootstrap CI on p95) for models with unusually high variance.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Minimum Sample Sizes and Windowing > Minimum samples (per key K, per window)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Minimum Sample Sizes and Windowing > Minimum samples (per key K, per window)
sections.content:
Minimum samples (per key K, per window)

- **Latency metrics**: minimum **200 successful canary requests** per window.
- **Tokens/sec**: minimum **200 successful canary requests** per window AND minimum **50,000 total generated tokens** per window.

If sample requirements are not met:

- No alert state change is allowed (prevents flapping in low-coverage periods).
- Dashboard panels display “insufficient sample” annotation.

Rationale:

- Tail latency (p95/p99) is unreliable with very small N.
- Tokens/sec needs sufficient token volume to smooth per-request variance.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Baseline Computation > Fixed baseline artifact
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Baseline Computation > Fixed baseline artifact
sections.content:
Baseline Computation

Fixed baseline artifact

- Source: controlled perf-canary runs using the approved synthetic prompt distribution.
- For each baseline key, we store:
  - distribution summaries (p50/p95/p99) for each latency metric
  - mean and standard deviation where stable enough to be meaningful
  - tokens/sec distribution summaries
  - run metadata (time range, sample count, canary config version)
- Baseline validity: baseline is considered valid only if it meets minimum sample size requirements (see below) and passes sanity checks (no telemetry gaps, no error-rate spikes).

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Appendix B: Ownership
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Appendix B: Ownership
sections.content:
Appendix B: Ownership

- Baseline pipeline and artifact integrity: Telemetry Platform (Logan Wright) + Metrics/Baselines (Nadia Rahman)
- Threshold standards and paging hygiene: SRE (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant)
- Model list and rollout gating integration: Serving Runtime (Noah Patel) + Release Engineering (Connor O'Brien)

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Consequences > Negative / Tradeoffs
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Consequences > Negative / Tradeoffs
sections.content:
Negative / Tradeoffs

- Requires baseline artifact generation whenever major runtime/kernel changes land for covered models/SKUs.
- Some true regressions may be detected slightly later due to sustained-breach requirements.
- Optional region/tier overrides add complexity when enabled.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Alternatives Considered > C) Per-region baselines always on
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Alternatives Considered > C) Per-region baselines always on
sections.content:
C) Per-region baselines always on

Pros:

- Reduces false positives due to cross-region fleet differences.

Cons:

- Baseline explosion (more artifacts and config), operational overhead.

Decision: Region is optional and only enabled for models/regions where observed variance requires it.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Consequences > Positive
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Consequences > Positive
sections.content:
Consequences

Positive

- Stable, versioned baselines support rollout gates and high-confidence paging.
- Rolling health baseline provides drift visibility without undermining safety.
- Anti-flap controls reduce alert noise and prevent incident-bot storms.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Telemetry delay protection
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Telemetry delay protection
sections.content:
Telemetry delay protection

If telemetry ingestion delay exceeds 2x the evaluation window (e.g., >20 minutes), alert evaluation is suspended and a separate “telemetry delay” warning is emitted to #eng-platform.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Alternatives Considered > B) Pure fixed baseline (never updated unless manual)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Alternatives Considered > B) Pure fixed baseline (never updated unless manual)
sections.content:
B) Pure fixed baseline (never updated unless manual)

Pros:

- Extremely stable; easy to reason about.

Cons:

- Becomes stale as fleet/hardware/driver changes accumulate; increases false positives over time.
- Forces frequent manual work to remain relevant.

Decision: Rejected as the only strategy. Adopted as primary baseline with explicit regeneration workflows.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Minimum Sample Sizes and Windowing > Evaluation window
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Minimum Sample Sizes and Windowing > Evaluation window
sections.content:
Minimum Sample Sizes and Windowing

Evaluation window

- Default evaluation window: **10 minutes**.
- Windows are evaluated continuously and require sustained breach rules (see anti-flap).

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Default Thresholds (v1) > Latency (p95 end-to-end)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Default Thresholds (v1) > Latency (p95 end-to-end)
sections.content:
Latency (p95 end-to-end)

- Warning: p95 E2E latency **+10%** vs baseline for **2 out of 3** consecutive evaluation windows.
- Paging: p95 E2E latency **+20%** vs baseline for **3 out of 4** consecutive evaluation windows.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Changelog
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Changelog
sections.content:
Changelog

- 2026-02-12: Clarified cooldown timers, added telemetry delay protection rule, and tightened tokens/sec minimum token count requirement.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Dedupe key
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Dedupe key
sections.content:
Dedupe key

Incident-bot dedupes based on:

- model_id + model_version + runtime_build_id + kernel_set_id + hardware_sku (+ region if present) + metric_type + severity

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Sustained breach logic
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Sustained breach logic
sections.content:
Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis

Sustained breach logic

We use “M out of N windows” to reduce sensitivity to transient spikes:

- Warning: 2/3 consecutive windows breach
- Paging: 3/4 consecutive windows breach

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Regression Definition
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Regression Definition
sections.content:
Regression Definition

We define regression as a statistically and operationally meaningful deviation from the fixed baseline.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Decision
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Decision
sections.content:
Decision

We adopt a **hybrid baseline strategy**:

1) **Primary baseline = Fixed, versioned baseline per (model, model_version, runtime_build, kernel_set_id, hardware_sku) with optional region override**

- Baselines are generated from controlled canary runs (prod-like load) and stored as immutable artifacts.
- Baselines are explicitly tied to the runtime build and kernel selection identifiers so comparisons remain meaningful.
- This is the baseline used for rollout gating and for paging.

2) **Secondary baseline = Rolling “health baseline” used for drift monitoring and threshold calibration (not for paging)**

- We compute a rolling reference from recent stable periods (default: last 7 days) to detect slow environmental drift and to inform recalibration.
- Rolling baseline is not used to auto-suppress a fixed-baseline regression; it is used as a triage and tuning signal.

3) **Baseline freeze rules**

- During a runtime rollout (canary/gradual), the baseline used for alerts is **frozen** to the most recent fixed baseline for the currently active runtime build on that ring.
- If an incident is declared for a perf regression, baseline updates are **paused** for affected keys until incident closure.

4) **Threshold evaluation requires minimum sample size + sustained breach + hysteresis**

- Alerts require both a minimum number of canary requests and sustained breach across multiple evaluation windows.
- Alert clear conditions are stricter than trigger conditions (hysteresis) to reduce flapping.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Default Thresholds (v1)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Default Thresholds (v1)
sections.content:
Default Thresholds (v1)

Thresholds are configurable per model, with these platform defaults used unless overridden.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Default Thresholds (v1) > Runtime-only attribution signals (non-paging by default)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Default Thresholds (v1) > Runtime-only attribution signals (non-paging by default)
sections.content:
Runtime-only attribution signals (non-paging by default)

These are emitted to dashboards and included in alert payloads, but do not page unless explicitly enabled for a model:

- Queueing time p95 +25% (suggests scheduler/fleet saturation)
- Prefill p95 +15% (suggests kernel/model config regressions)
- Decode p95 +15% (suggests kernel/model config regressions)

Rationale:

- Paging should be driven by end-to-end customer-impact proxy (E2E p95 and tokens/sec).
- Breakdown metrics improve triage but are often noisier and more sensitive to load mix.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Default Thresholds (v1) > Throughput (tokens/sec)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Default Thresholds (v1) > Throughput (tokens/sec)
sections.content:
Throughput (tokens/sec)

- Warning: tokens/sec **-8%** vs baseline for **2 out of 3** windows.
- Paging: tokens/sec **-15%** vs baseline for **3 out of 4** windows.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Regression Definition > Threshold levels
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Regression Definition > Threshold levels
sections.content:
Threshold levels

Two alert levels exist:

- **Warning**: actionable signal for runtime team triage; routed to #eng-runtime.
- **Paging**: sustained, high-confidence regression on top models; routed to on-call rotation.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Rollout Guidance
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Rollout Guidance
sections.content:
Rollout Guidance

- Phase 1 (single region): warnings only, tune per-model overrides until noise is acceptable.
- Phase 2: enable paging only for top models with proven low variance and stable baselines.
- Phase 3: integrate gating with release engineering once paging signal is trusted (warning can gate early as “soft fail,” paging as “hard fail”).

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Alert clear (hysteresis)
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Alert clear (hysteresis)
sections.content:
Alert clear (hysteresis)

Alerts clear only when performance returns closer to baseline:

- Warning clears when Δ < +6% (latency) and Δ > -5% (tokens/sec) for 3/3 windows.
- Paging clears when Δ < +12% (latency) and Δ > -10% (tokens/sec) for 4/4 windows.

sections.section_path: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Cooldown
sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Anti-Flap, Dedupe, and Hysteresis > Cooldown
sections.content:
Cooldown

After an alert transitions to firing, we enforce a cooldown before re-triggering a new incident thread for the same key:

- Warning cooldown: 60 minutes
- Paging cooldown: 120 minutes

sections.content:
Runbook Writing And Telemetry Bootcamp Curriculum 2026

Source type: confluence
Document ID: dsid_46a4cb87db414e769f2df86f01626948
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Runbook Writing and Telemetry Bootcamp Curriculum — Operator Training

Summary

This page documents a repeatable, instructor-led bootcamp to train platform operators and engineers to write high-quality runbooks that are telemetry-driven, testable, and maintainable. The curriculum is designed for new operators, service owners, and incident responders who will author or own runbooks for platform services (prefix cache, allocator, tenant-slicing, model-variant router).

Audience

- Platform operators and SREs
- Service owners in eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime
- Oncall engineers who respond to latency/cost incidents

Learning objectives (measurable)

1. Produce a runbook that contains a clear escalation path, data-driven detection predicates, and an operator checklist.
2. Write two telemetry queries (one metric-based, one log-based) that reliably surface the condition the runbook describes.
3. Create a synthetic verification (unit) that validates the runbook’s detection predicates against a small replay dataset.
4. Implement a post-incident update cycle and link to the action in the runbook so it can be closed by the owner.

Curriculum overview (3-day instructor-led)
Day 0 — Prework (self-paced)

- Read: "Runbook authoring and maintenance guidelines" (required).
- Complete a short quiz on SLO definitions and common platform failure modes.
- Setup: access to Grafana/Tempo, Kibana, and a sandbox tenant. Confirm permissions with infra-oncall.

Day 1 — Foundations and detection

- Morning: Lecture (1.5 hr) — Runbook structure and the telemetry-first principle.
  - Sections: Summary, Impact, Detection (metric + log predicates), Immediate actions, Escalation, Rollback, Postmortem link.
  - Example services: kv-prefix-cache, dynamic-allocator, model-variant-router.
- Lab (2.5 hr): Write detection predicates for a synthetic latency spike:
  1) Metric predicate: p95 latency > 300ms for 5m AND error rate > 1% for 2m.
  2) Log predicate: queries that include "kv-cache:miss" and "eviction-reason=reshuffle" for >50 events in 10m.
- Homework: Author a first draft runbook for a provided scenario.

Day 2 — Triage, actions, and testability

- Morning: Workshop (2 hr) — Mapping telemetry to operator actions.
  - Instrumentation checklist: SLI names, tag conventions (region, tenant_id, model_variant), and minimum retention expectations (30 days for alerts, 90 days for postmortem traces).
  - Ownership patterns: primary, secondary, oncall-runbook-maintainer.
- Lab (3 hr): Implement a synthetic verification for the runbook detection predicates using the synthetic-replay harness.
  - Deliverable: three test cases (baseline, transient spike, persistent degradation).
- Evening: Peer review session — teams exchange runbooks and provide 3 actionable comments.

Day 3 — Escalation, de-escalation, and lifecycle

- Morning: Tabletop simulation (2 hr) — live incident with operator rotation. Measured outcomes: time to detection, time to mitigate, number of escalations, checklist completeness.
- Afternoon: Retrospective (1.5 hr) — calibrate SLOs and adjust detection thresholds.
- Closing: Runbook merge checklist and post-incident update procedure.

Assessment and certification

- Pass criteria: runbook accepted in repo (PR merged), synthetic verification green, and at least one successful tabletop participation.
- Certificate: "Telemetry-Driven Runbook Author (Redwood)" valid for 18 months. Re-certification: 2-hour refresher + one tabletop.

Delivery model and resourcing

sections.section_path: Runbook Writing And Telemetry Bootcamp Curriculum 2026
sections.heading: Runbook Writing And Telemetry Bootcamp Curriculum 2026
sections.content:
- Instructor: Platform training lead (approx. 1 dedicated trainer per cohort of 12).
- Duration: 3 days (24 total hours including pre/post work).
- Environment: sandbox cluster with one copy of kv-prefix-cache and dynamic-allocator seeded with synthetic load.
- Tools: Grafana (dashboards pre-built), Loki/Kibana, Tempo (trace slices), synthetic-replay harness (repo: infra/synthetic-replay).

Runbook template (required fields)
1) Title (single line)
2) Summary (1–2 sentences) — short impact statement
3) Owner (primary, secondary) — team and pager alias
4) Impact and user-visible symptoms — list
5) Detection

   - Metric predicate (exact expression)
   - Log predicate (example query)
   - Trace pattern (optional)

6) Immediate mitigation steps (numbered)
7) Escalation path (names/roles and contact method)
8) Safe rollback / service-level de-escalation (how to revert changes)
9) Diagnostics checklist (commands, queries, dashboard links)
10) Post-incident required actions (TTR SLA for update: 7 days)
11) Verification tests (links to synthetic tests)
12) Related runbooks and runbook-ids
Required telemetry examples (copyable)

- Metric predicate (PromQL):
  sum(rate(request_duration_ms_bucket{job="kv-prefix-cache",le="0.3"}[5m])) by (region) / sum(rate(request_duration_ms_count{job="kv-prefix-cache"}[5m])) by (region) > 0.95
- Log predicate (Loki):
  {app="kv-prefix-cache",env="prod"} |= "kv-cache:miss" | json | tenant_id!="" | count_over_time(10m) > 50
- Trace predicate (Tempo/trace): search for spans with operation.name =~ "kv-prefix-cache.*evict" and duration > 100ms, aggregated by tenant_id.

Synthetic verification example (bash)

- Reproduce a persistent-degradation case with synthetic-replay:
  1) ./synthetic-replay --scenario=kv-cache-eviction-heavy --duration=15m --tenants=10
  2) Wait for PromQL predicate to evaluate true in the sandbox (check metrics-exporter).
  3) Run owner diagnostics script: tools/diagnostics/kv-cache-inspect.sh --tenant <id>

Tabletop scenarios (catalog)

- KV cache shard reshuffle during black-box warmup
- Region-specific allocator starvation (spot preemption cascade)
- Model-variant fallback thrash causing token-cost spikes
- Multi-tenant cold-cache cold-start causing onboarding failures

Retention and SLO guidance for runbooks

- Telemetry retention required for runbook validation: metrics 30d, logs 90d, traces 90d.
- Alert SLO: detection-to-acknowledge median <= 3m for SEV2, median <= 1m for SEV1 during business hours.
- Escalation target: oncall primary owns initial mitigation within 15m of alert for SEV1.

Merge checklist (PR to runbook repo)

1) Runbook filled using template and linked to service metadata (service ID, repo).
2) At least one synthetic verification included and green in CI.
3) Two reviewers from different teams approved (one operator, one service owner).
4) Dashboard links present and dashboards annotated with threshold panels.

Ownership and follow-up

- Course owner: Priya Kapoor (eng-platform training). Contact: priya@redwood.ai (internal).
- Curriculum reviewers: see metadata above.
- Quarterly review: curriculum and scenario catalog reviewed each quarter; runbook templates updated at least annually.

Appendix A — Example telemetry queries and dashboard panels

- Grafana panel: "kv-prefix-cache p95 by region"
  - PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_ms_bucket{job=\"kv-prefix-cache\"}[5m])) by (le, region))
- Alert rule: "kv-cache-p95-region-high"
  - Expression: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_ms_bucket{job=\"kv-prefix-cache\"}[5m])) by (le, region)) > 0.3
  - For: 5m, Labels: severity=SEV2, owner=kv-cache-team

- Example debug command (operator):
  - kubectl -n platform logs -l app=kv-prefix-cache --since=15m | jq -r '.message' | grep eviction

Related pages and templates

- Runbook authoring guidelines (required pre-read) — /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/runbook-authoring-and-maintenance-guidelines-2025
- Synthetic-replay repository — infra/synthetic-replay (internal git)

Revision history

sections.section_path: Int 460811 Edge Switch Arp Proxy Ip Duplication
sections.heading: Int 460811 Edge Switch Arp Proxy Ip Duplication
sections.content:
Issue summary: Several users reporting intermittent loss of access to internal services while connected to corporate VPN. Symptoms include duplicate IP conflict alerts on endpoints, frequent VPN re-auth events, and traffic appearing to be routed to a different on-prem host (service 10.23.5.12). Impact: ~8% of VPN sessions in us-west over the last 48h experienced short blackholes (30-90s) impacting git pushes, internal CI jobs, and ssh sessions. Scope: affects users on Wi-Fi SSID 'Redwood-Corp' behind specific edge switches in building SF2 rack 7.
1) Connect laptop to 'Redwood-Corp' Wi-Fi in SF2 building (tested on macOS 13 and Ubuntu 22.04)
2) Establish VPN session to redwood-vpn-usw.redwood.net (WireGuard-based corporate VPN)
3) Trigger continuous ping to an internal host (ping -i 0.2 10.23.5.12)
4) Observe intermittent duplicate IP warnings on client and packets forwarded to an unexpected MAC on the L2 domain
5) Reproduce frequency increases when there is a short burst of multicast/mDNS traffic on the same AP's radio
Client syslog excerpt: 'kernel: arp: IP address 10.23.8.45 claimed by 00:11:22:33:44:55 (conflict)'
Switch (edge-sw-7) log: 'proxy-arp conflict detected for 10.23.8.45, source 00:66:77:88:99:AA bridging-port 5'
Packet capture (pcap) snippet: ARP reply for 10.23.8.45 with two different source MACs within 120ms
VPN server metrics: client rekey count spike (client 10.23.8.45) correlated to timestamp 2026-03-12T14:12Z
Internal service (10.23.5.12) reported TCP reset spikes aligning with client blackholes
Hypothesis 1: Edge switch proxy-arp configured for legacy NAT path is responding to ARP for VPN-assigned addresses from an overlapping DHCP pool, causing two active ARP entries on the LAN.
Hypothesis 2: A misconfigured VXLAN/bridge on edge-sw-7 is advertising ARP for the VPN subnet into the campus L2 segment when multicast bursts occur.
What we tried: - Disabled proxy-arp on edge-sw-7 port-channel to AP group temporarily (no immediate reduction). - Isolated a suspect AP by moving a test client to a different AP (blackhole persisted only when client served by AP-7A). - Captured pcap on AP, switch uplink, and VPN server concurrently for correlated timestamps (pcaps saved to /mnt/logs/INT-460811/pcaps/).
Preliminary find: ARP 'gratuitous' replies with VPN client IP are being injected by the switch's 'proxy-arp' feature only when the AP's multicast queue exceeds threshold. The switch returns ARP for the same IP with a different MAC that matches a spare management interface in rack 7 (00:66:77:88:99:AA).
Intermittent connectivity loss for internal developer workflows (git/ssh/CI). Approximately 8% of VPN sessions in the SF2 us-west site affected in the window; potential for data-transfer retries and CI flakiness. No customer-facing outage but notable developer productivity hit.
1) Placed affected edge switch (edge-sw-7) in monitoring schedule and enabled debug logging for proxy-arp events.
2) Temporarily increased DHCP lease affinity for VPN pool for clients in SF2 to reduce the window for IP reuse.
3) Asked campus networking team to disable 'proxy-arp' global feature on a staging switch and observe (ongoing).
4) Notified platform reliability and CI owners of potential re-run needs for impacted jobs (Slack #incidents and #platform-alerts).
2026-03-11 09:18 - Jonah Reed: Assigned to network; will coordinate switch config changes and gather pcaps. Next action: schedule maintenance window if we need to push config rollback.

sections.heading: Int 460811 Edge Switch Arp Proxy Ip Duplication
sections.content:
2026-03-12 15:25 - Priya Shah (campus-net): Reproduced proxy-arp responses on edge-sw-7 when AP multicast queue > 70%. Suspect firmware 1.2.3 on these switches has a known misc bridging bug. Opened ticket with vendor (TAC-889233).
2026-03-13 08:52 - Jonah Reed: Vendor TAC confirmed the switch may respond to ARP for non-local subnets under multicast overload in 1.2.3. Recommended immediate mitigation: set 'proxy-arp disable' on VRF for AP VLANs and upgrade firmware to 1.2.6.
2026-03-14 07:30 - Aisha Malik: Applied 'proxy-arp disable' to edge-sw-7 in staged maintenance window (07:00-07:15). Monitoring: VPN rekey spikes reduced from 47/hr to 2/hr for affected clients in the first 24h.
2026-03-14 10:02 - Jonah Reed: Confirming RFC and rollout plan for global fix. Proposed follow-up: firmware upgrade across SF2 rack 4-9, audit for proxy-arp enabled on other edge switches, and update config baseline to explicitly disable proxy-arp for VPN/DHCP subnets.
Switch firmware (1.2.3) bug caused proxy-arp behavior under high multicast load leading to ARP advertisements for VPN-assigned addresses. This created ephemeral duplicate IP assignments on the L2 domain and caused VPN clients to experience routing blackholes and rekeys.
Mitigation applied: 'proxy-arp disable' set on edge-sw-7 AP VLANs during maintenance window 2026-03-14 07:00-07:15.
Temporary workaround: increased DHCP lease affinity and moved high-multicast APs to separate RF profile to reduce multicast bursts.
Permanent fix: planned firmware upgrade to 1.2.6 across SF2 edge switches (racks 4-9) and config baseline change to disable proxy-arp for VPN/DHCP subnets. Vendor TAC provided patch notes and recommended upgrade path.
Follow-ups: - Create change request CR-2026-0415 for firmware rollout. - Run campus-wide audit script to detect 'proxy-arp' enabled instances and remediate. - Add regression test to onboarding checklist for AP multicast stress.
Status: Partial fix applied and validated; full remediation scheduled (see CR-2026-0415).

sections.heading: Int 738205 Wifi Bridge Nat Source Rewrite Breaks Vpn Policy
sections.content:
Int 738205 Wifi Bridge Nat Source Rewrite Breaks Vpn Policy

Source type: jira
Document ID: dsid_e728a420a02a4ddcb125e6adb09d211e
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Office edge bridge in NAT mode rewriting source IPs and causing VPN policy routing failures and SSO timeouts

Issue summary: After a recent office CAB change at the SoMa satellite office we started seeing a sustained increase in VPN session failures and SSO timeouts for users on the office Wi‑Fi. Impact: ~12-18% of users at SoMa experience intermittent 403/SSO timeouts or are unable to reach internal services that normally resolve via VPN private IPs. Service impact is localized to the office LAN and affects employees using company Wi‑Fi and a subset of developer services behind policy-based routing. Initial hypothesis: an intermediate bridge/AP that was re-provisioned to 'NAT' mode is rewriting source addresses causing VPN policy lookup to fail, triggering mis-routed traffic and SSO token validation errors.
1) Connect a laptop to SoMa corporate Wi‑Fi (ssid: Redwood-Corp).
2) Establish Redwood VPN (WireGuard client) and authenticate via SSO (Okta).
3) Attempt to curl an internal service at 10.11.20.5: expect success; observed: connection resets or 403 responses.
4) Observe device local IP (e.g., 192.168.50.34) and the outbound NATed IP as seen by internal services (packets show 10.100.200.1 source after NAT rewrite).
Clients on office Wi‑Fi see internal service requests fail intermittently. Packet captures from service frontends show source IPs mapped to 10.100.200.0/24 (bridge appliance SNAT pool) instead of clients' VPN-assigned 10.8.0.0/16 addresses. Okta SSO validation rejects token assertions when source IP does not match expected corporate ranges, causing auth flows to fail.
Traffic from VPN clients should preserve VPN-assigned source addresses. Office bridge should be in passthrough mode for tunneled traffic so policy-based routing at the gateway can correctly match flows and SSO sees expected IP ranges.
2026-03-10T09:22:13Z firewall[gw-usw-1]: policy_lookup: src=10.8.12.45 dst=10.11.20.5 matched=internal-web-cluster action=allow
2026-03-10T09:22:13Z app-fw[web-01]: tcpdump: in.ether src=10.100.200.14:52344 > 10.11.20.5:443 SYN
2026-03-10T09:23:01Z okta-proxy[auth-01]: token_validation: ip_mismatch user=jared@example.com expected_range=10.8.0.0/16 seen_ip=10.100.200.14

- Confirmed bridge device model: Ubiquiti UBB‑Edge v2 (serial: UB-1212). Reprovisioning on 2026-03-09 set its WAN mode to 'Gateway (NAT)' instead of 'Bridge'.
- tcpdump on web-01 shows multiple connections with SNATed sources 10.100.200.0/24. When testing from a home client via remote VPN this does not occur; home clients preserve 10.8.x source addresses.
- ip rule list on gw-usw-1 shows policy routing keyed on src network 10.8.0.0/16. Because SNAT rewrote source to 10.100.200.x the kernel falls back to default route and packets get dropped or mis-routed to edge ACLs.
- Quick check: ssh to bridge admin UI -> Network -> NAT Mode = Enabled. CLI 'iptables -t nat -L -n' shows POSTROUTING MASQUERADE for bridge LAN range.
- Hypothesis validated by temporary change: disabled NAT on bridge -> source IPs preserved -> internal service connectivity restored and SSO token validations succeed.

As an immediate mitigation, network ops applied a bridge-level configuration that disables MASQUERADE for src 10.8.0.0/16 which restored service for all connected clients.

Gpu Ci Credential Rotation And Image Promotion Safety

Source type: confluence
Document ID: dsid_f1b208f3637e4987aeab371242a5bea5
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
GPU CI credential rotation and image promotion safety kit

Summary
Purpose
This document defines a safety-first pattern for: (1) rotating CI credentials used by GPU provisioning and image-promotion pipelines, and (2) promoting GPU runtime images (golden bundles) to production pools with provable checks and fast rollback paths. The kit bundles Terraform/IaC patterns, CI job templates, runtime verification checks, SLO-driven gating, and an operator runbook for emergency credential revocation.

Why this matters

- Credential rotation without careful orchestration can leave running inference pools unable to pull images, causing degraded capacity and failed deployments.
- Image promotion (CI -> staging -> prod) must be atomic and verifiable: a mismatched image in a GPU pool can produce model-regression incidents.
- Past incidents show the majority of image-promotion outages occur during key rotation + cross-account image copy windows. This doc reduces blast radius.

Scope
Applies to: all CI pipelines that build GPU runtime images, the Terraform modules that provision tenant GPU hosts and warm pools, and the image-signing/attestation services used by Redwood Inference.

Owner and contacts

- Owner team: engineering (Infra Reliability)
- Primary oncall for rollout windows: infra-oncall@redwood.com
- Escalation: Diego Ramos (Lead - GPU Infra), Priya Shah (Security), Evan Liu (CI/CD)

Terminology

- Golden image: signed OCI image bundle used for production inference nodes.
- Image promoter: CI job that signs, copies, and tags artifacts into the production registry.
- Promotion window: the short period where an image transitions from staging to prod and cross-account copies may be in-flight.

Safety principles (high level)
1) Always sign images with key versioning (KMS key alias + key-id). Verification must include key version metadata.
2) Use a promotion plan that stages in-region canaries before full fleet promotion.
3) Make credential rotation a two-phase operation: preflight (test) then swap (cutover) with automatic rollback on failure.
4) Prefer short-lived credentials (ephemeral IAM role / signed cert) for CI agents; store long-term secrets only in HSM-backed KMS.
5) Maintain an explicit PROMOTION SAFETY MATRIX mapping signals to actions (below).

Promotion safety matrix\

| Signal | Threshold | Action | Rollback trigger |
|--------|-----------:|--------|-----------------|
| Canary 99th latency increase | +40% vs baseline | Halt promotion, mark image suspect, run deeper perf trace | Auto-revert to previous tag in 15m if >2 buckets exceed threshold |
| Error rate (5xx) | >0.5% absolute | Re-route 100% traffic off canary nodes, abort promotion | Full fleet rollback if persisted for 10m |
| Tokenization mismatch (new tokenizer failure) | any runtime error | Halt; capture failing prompt, block image | Manual rollback after investigation |
| Image signature verification failures | any | Stop promotion, alert security, revoke CI key version | Block until signature chain validated |
| Pull auth errors across >=2 regions | >=3% pull failures | Pause promotion; force ephemeral credential refresh | If persists 10m, automated rollback and revoke ephemeral role |

sections.section_path: Gpu Ci Credential Rotation And Image Promotion Safety
sections.heading: Gpu Ci Credential Rotation And Image Promotion Safety
sections.content:
Preflight checklist (CI + Terraform)
1) CI builds image and signs with signing service (key alias: kms/gpu-image-signer). Artifact metadata must include key-version and build-id.
2) CI runs integration smoke: small inference harness against a staging warm pool (tag: staging-smoke). Verify latency and correctness metrics.
3) Terraform plan for registry permissions and cross-account roles is generated and reviewed via tfsec/gate. Module names referenced: tf-modules/registry-crosscopy, tf-modules/ephemeral-ci-role, tf-modules/warm-pool-provisioner.
4) Register promotion intent in the promotion ledger (tagged Git commit + promotion ticket).

CI pipeline example (GitHub Actions / Buildkite style)

- name: build-and-sign-gpu-image
  runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
  steps:
    - checkout
    - run: |
        docker build -t staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}} -f infra/Dockerfile .
        docker push staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}}
    - uses: redwood/sign-image-action@v1
      with:
        image: staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}}
        kms-key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/gpu/cryptoKeys/gpu-image-signer
    - run: |
        curl -X POST https://signing.redwood.internal/attest -d '{"image":"staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}}","key_version":"v3"}'

Promotion job (partial)

- name: promote-to-canary
  env:
    EPHEMERAL_ROLE_ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-ephemeral-publisher
  steps:
    - assume-role $EPHEMERAL_ROLE_ARN --duration 900
    - run: |
        ./scripts/cross-account-copy --src staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}} --dst prod-gpu:${{PROMOTION_TAG}} --regions us-west-2,eu-west-1
    - run: |
        terraform -chdir=infra/promotion apply -auto-approve -var='image_tag=${PROMOTION_TAG}'

Terraform patterns and recommendations

- Module: registry-crosscopy
  - Purpose: declaratively model cross-account ECR/GCR copy permissions and a short-lived promotion task.
  - Inputs: src_repo, dst_repo, allowed_regions, promotion_role_arn
  - Outputs: promotion_task_id, crosscopy_logs_s3
- Module: ephemeral-ci-role
  - Purpose: create an IAM role the CI system assumes for promotion. Short-lived session only; require MFA for manual triggers. Use OPA policy to prevent wide-scoped permissions.
- Remote state gating: the promotion apply must assert a remote state lock and include a semaphore key in a central tfstate bucket to avoid concurrent promotions.

Credential rotation protocol (two-phase)
Phase A: Preflight (no live swap)
1) Provision new KMS key version and create alias kms/gpu-image-signer -> key-vN.
2) Deploy CI adapters (sign-image-action) to use key-vN in a feature-flagged mode and run 100% test-signings that do not change promotion ledger. Verify that attestation services accept key-vN signatures.
3) Run shadow cross-account copy with ephemeral role using new signing metadata. Confirm copies succeed across all target regions.
4) Monitor for 24h (or 3 release windows) for any unexpected pull auth regressions.

Phase B: Cutover (the swap)
1) Schedule change window (SLO: <30m blind window).
2) Update alias kms/gpu-image-signer -> key-vN (atomic alias swap).
3) Revoke short-lived CI credentials associated with key-v(N-1) after 5m grace. Rotate ephemeral role sessions.
4) Promote a canary image signed with key-vN. Verify canary health for 20m across latency/error metrics.
5) Proceed to full fleet promotion if no triggers fired; otherwise, revert alias to key-v(N-1) and mark key-vN as revocation-pending for forensic review.

Emergency rollback runbook (oncall steps)
1) Detect: Pager fires for pull auth failures or mass pod CrashLoopBackOff when pulling prod images.
2) Immediate action (within first 5 minutes):

   - Confirm via cross-region registry metrics whether pull auth errors are present and their percentage.
   - If pull auth failures >=3% across >=2 regions, run: ./scripts/revoke-ci-ephemeral-sessions --role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-ephemeral-publisher
   - If image signature mismatch reported, quarantine the image tag: mark in the promotion ledger as blocked.

3) If problems persist >10m:

sections.section_path: Gpu Ci Credential Rotation And Image Promotion Safety
sections.heading: Gpu Ci Credential Rotation And Image Promotion Safety
sections.content:
- Revert registry image tag on affected warm pools to previous production tag via terraform apply -var='image_tag=${PREV_TAG}'
   - Recreate node groups (if nodes are stuck) by triggering warm-pool rolling-replace job.

4) Post-incident: open an incident review, attach promotion ledger entries, CI logs, KMS audit trail, and the short-lived session token logs.

Observability and SLOs to enforce

- Canary latency delta SLO: canary 99th must stay within +25% of baseline during canary window.
- Image pull success: >=99.5% successful pulls within 1m of request at steady state.
- Promotion lead time: preflight checks must finish within 90 minutes for standard releases; emergencies may use expedited path with manual approver.

Telemetry dashboards (must include)

- Registry pull success rate by region and account (1m and 5m windows)
- Image signature verification failures by key-version
- Promotion job success/failure histogram (by commit)
- Canary latency and error rate trends vs baseline (auto-annotate promotion events)

Automation safety checks (required CI gates)

- Signatures must be validated by attestation service and include key-version metadata. Job fails on mismatches.
- OPA admission check in promotion Terraform that asserts promotion_task_id is unique and no concurrent promotions are in progress.
- Pre-promotion smoke harness that runs 100 inference prompts and validates outputs against a golden-response set (fuzzy matching allowed; threshold 95% similarity).

FAQ and edge cases
Q: What if a region's image copy lags by more than 30 minutes?
A: Pause promotion and trigger a manual crosscopy re-run. If unable to copy within 60 minutes, postpone full promotion and continue with a limited regional promotion strategy.

Q: Who can manually trigger expedited promotions?
A: CI admins with MFA + a signed approval from the Release Lead and Security. The ephemeral role requires an MFA assertion to be assumed for manual flows.

Appendix A — Example Terraform stub for ephemeral role
resource "aws_iam_role" "ci_ephemeral_publisher" {
  name               = "ci-ephemeral-publisher-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume.json
  tags = { team = "gpu-infra", created_by = "ci-pipeline" }
}

sections.section_path: deny if concurrent_promotion == true
sections.heading: deny if concurrent_promotion == true
sections.content:
OPA policy (promotion gate) — high level

deny if concurrent_promotion == true

package promotion.gate
default allow = false
allow {
  not input.concurrent_promotion
}

- 2024-02-15: Initial draft (Asha Patel)
- 2024-04-10: Added KMS two-phase rotation guidance and example CI snippets (review: Diego Ramos)
- 2024-06-03: Updated safety thresholds and rollback timing after postmortem lessons (review: Priya Shah)

Related resources

- tf-modules/registry-crosscopy README in repo infra/modules (link internal)
- signing.redwood.internal (image attestation service)
- infra/runbooks/warm-pool-rolling-replace-runbook.json

Acknowledgements
Thanks to Diego Ramos, Priya Shah, Evan Liu, and the Release Engineering rotation team for review and early testing.
