From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, May 20, 2025 at 11:06 AM
Subject: Re: Trident — DPA/SLA redlines (need positions today)

Quick take (security/compliance):
A) Residency

- For Private (VPC), we can commit that customer content (prompts/outputs) is processed and stored within the deployed region/VPC per the architecture. We should NOT commit that “no Redwood personnel outside US can ever access.” Better: access is controlled, logged, and limited to authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis; remote access can be restricted by customer policy in the Private deployment.
- Subprocessors: in Private/VPC, this is largely their cloud provider + any Redwood support tooling (if enabled). We should require a defined list / allow updates with notice.

B) Retention

- Separate: (1) customer content retention vs (2) operational/audit logs.
- We can offer “no training on customer data” language if not already in the DPA; and for retention, propose “customer-configurable retention settings; default per product; can be set to short windows; deletion upon request subject to legal/operational requirements.”
- 24 hours hard SLA on deletion is tough; propose “within 30 days” standard, with best efforts for faster.

C) Audit logs / SIEM export

- We can support audit logging and export. We should counter that 7-year retention is on customer side (their SIEM). We can commit we provide log export and the customer can retain as long as they need.

D) Incident notice

- Recommend counter: notify without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of confirmation of a Security Incident affecting Customer Data.
- If business wants to concede: 48 hours post-confirmation for “confirmed material incidents.”

I can help wordsmith but need Sofia/legal to decide positions.

Naomi

Strongly recommend we avoid absolute commitments that could be interpreted as “no cross-border access ever.” We can commit to:

- access controls (RBAC), MFA/SSO where applicable, and auditability of admin actions;

sections.section_path: 2026 01 16 Gcp Marketplace Onboarding And Billing Review
sections.heading: 2026 01 16 Gcp Marketplace Onboarding And Billing Review
sections.content:
[00:33] Chris Osei: Yep, and I’m Chris, program lead on our side for the marketplace refresh. I’ll keep us on agenda and capture action items.

[00:41] Anika Desai: Hi all. Anika, partner engineering. I can talk through entitlement, procurement IDs, and the typical “gotchas” we see when SaaS vendors wire up the onboarding.

[00:50] Miguel Alvarez: Miguel here. Cloud Commerce metering / billing integrations. Happy to go deep on dimensions, aggregation, rounding, and what reviewers will look for.

[01:01] Stephanie Nguyen: Great. Quick context: we’re replacing legacy listings. We now have Hosted API usage-based, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployment. We want the marketplace SKUs to map cleanly to our internal billing meters. The primary issues we want to avoid are dimension mismatches and the buyer gets invoiced for something weird.

[01:20] Miguel Alvarez: Yeah. The big thing is consistency. Dimension names and IDs in the offer need to match what you’re sending in metering events. And be careful if you’re changing them later—customers don’t like it and it can break reporting.

[01:35] Cole Summers: That’s exactly what we’re trying to nail. Let me outline what we were thinking and you can tell us what’s realistic. For Hosted, we meter “tokens generated” and “input tokens” internally, but we can expose it as “tokens” total if that’s simpler. We also have embeddings measured as “embedding units” (basically per 1K tokens equivalent). For Dedicated, we have reserved GPU capacity, which internally is monthly commit + overage. Private is more of a platform fee plus support tier.

[02:05] Miguel Alvarez: Okay. So in Cloud Marketplace, you can do usage-based dimensions and you can do subscription pricing models, and you can also do committed-use style constructs depending on the product type. Most SaaS partners keep it simple: one or a small number of usage dimensions, like “1K tokens” or “1M tokens”, and then for a base subscription you do a seat or a flat monthly fee.

[02:29] Nadia Rahman: Quick question on granularity. If we do “1K tokens” as the unit, do you see partners reporting fractional quantities? Like 123.456 units? Or is it recommended to round?

[02:41] Miguel Alvarez: You can send decimal quantities, but you should document how you compute it and be consistent. The most common pattern is you aggregate per hour or per day and send integer quantities. But for token meters, lots of folks send decimals, just be explicit. Rounding differences between your UI and the invoice is where support tickets come from.

[03:02] Ben Carter: On the onboarding side, we have this subscription -> entitlement -> Redwood org provisioning. One issue we see on AWS is entitlements sometimes take a few minutes to show up. Is that also a thing on GCP?

[03:14] Anika Desai: Yep. It’s not usually super long, but there can be propagation delay. The UX expectation is you handle “pending” gracefully. Like, don’t show a scary error that says “you are not entitled.” Instead say “we’re still syncing your subscription, retry in a few minutes” and maybe a refresh button.

sections.section_path: Adr 007 Kms Client Wrapper And Failure Policy > Decision > Decision 3: Timeouts and retry budgets are explicit and bounded > Default timeout and retry policy (safe defaults)
sections.heading: Adr 007 Kms Client Wrapper And Failure Policy > Decision > Decision 3: Timeouts and retry budgets are explicit and bounded > Default timeout and retry policy (safe defaults)
sections.content:
Default timeout and retry policy (safe defaults)

All values below are defaults; services may tighten them (stricter) without approval. Loosening them requires an explicit override with Security + SRE review.

| Operation | Default per-attempt timeout | Max attempts | Total time budget (cap) | Retry on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `Decrypt` | 750ms | 2 | 1.5s | `KMS_THROTTLED`, `KMS_TIMEOUT`, `KMS_TRANSIENT` |
| `Encrypt` | 750ms | 2 | 1.5s | `KMS_THROTTLED`, `KMS_TIMEOUT`, `KMS_TRANSIENT` |
| `GenerateDataKey` | 1.0s | 2 | 2.0s | `KMS_THROTTLED`, `KMS_TIMEOUT`, `KMS_TRANSIENT` |
| `GetKeyMetadata` / key lookup | 500ms | 2 | 1.0s | `KMS_THROTTLED`, `KMS_TIMEOUT`, `KMS_TRANSIENT` |

Backoff: exponential with full jitter.

- Initial delay: 50ms
- Max delay: 300ms
- Jitter: required
- Respect `Retry-After` where provided (bounded by total time budget)

Retry is explicitly disabled for non-retryable categories (`KMS_ACCESS_DENIED`, `KMS_NOT_FOUND`, `KMS_INVALID_CIPHERTEXT`, `KMS_KEY_DISABLED`, `KMS_MISCONFIGURED`).

sections.heading: Adr Perf Canary Baseline And Thresholds > Default Thresholds (v1) > Runtime-only attribution signals (non-paging by default)
sections.content:
Runtime-only attribution signals (non-paging by default)

These are emitted to dashboards and included in alert payloads, but do not page unless explicitly enabled for a model:

- Queueing time p95 +25% (suggests scheduler/fleet saturation)
- Prefill p95 +15% (suggests kernel/model config regressions)
- Decode p95 +15% (suggests kernel/model config regressions)

Rationale:

- Paging should be driven by end-to-end customer-impact proxy (E2E p95 and tokens/sec).
- Breakdown metrics improve triage but are often noisier and more sensitive to load mix.

Cross-role Tool Access Governance and Self-Service Handbook

Summary:

This handbook defines the governance model, operational runbook, and self-service flows for granting, reviewing, and revoking access to Redwood’s internal tools across roles and teams. It is intended for people-ops, engineering managers, security reviewers, and tool maintainers. The goal is to make tool access predictable, auditable, and fast while minimizing over-permissioning.

Key Principles:

- Least privilege by default: users receive the minimum role required to do their job.
- Role-driven access: we prefer role-based assignments with ephemeral exceptions.
- Self-service first, manual oversight when necessary: automate safe, common grants.
- Clear ownership: every tool has an owner and an escalation path.
- Auditable lifecycle: provisioning, reviews and deprovisioning are tracked centrally.

1) Scope and Definitions

- Tool: any internal SaaS, self-hosted service, or repo that requires explicit credentials or permissions (examples: AWS consoles, Jira admin groups, prod Grafana, CI pipelines).
- Role: a named collection of permissions (e.g., developer-readonly, infra-operator).
- Access Request: a request submitted to the Access Portal for a role or tool-specific permission.
- Exception: temporary access outside standard roles; must have an expiration and approver.

2) Ownership and Responsibilities

- Tool Owner (team-specified): maintains the role catalog, documents required permissions, defines safe self-service gates, and responds to escalations.
- People Ops: owns onboarding/offboarding orchestration, periodic review cadence, and highest-level policy.
- Security: defines acceptable exception policies, approves high-risk tools, and performs audits.
- Manager (requester approver): verifies business need and ties access to role/mission.

3) Access Model (high level)

- Role Catalog: canonical list of roles for common tools; stored in the Access Portal.
- Self-Service Roles: low-risk roles that can be assigned instantly (examples: docs-edit, ci-reader)
- Request-and-Approve Roles: medium-risk roles requiring manager approval (examples: staging-deploy, metrics-writer)
- Manual Approval Roles: high-risk roles requiring security review (examples: prod-admin, billing-admin)

4) Standard Provisioning Flow (Self-Service preferred)

1. User initiates request via Access Portal (or CLI).
2. For self-service roles: immediate grant recorded in audit log; user notified.
3. For manager-approval roles: manager receives approval email and must respond within 48 business hours; if approved, provisioning executes automatically.
4. For security-approval roles: security reviewer staged; expected SLA is 3 business days.
5. All grants include metadata: requester, approver, justification, expiration (if exception), and ticket ID.

5) Approval Matrix (sample)

| Tool Category | Example Tools | Typical Role Name | Approval Path | Max SLA for Approval | Expiration Policy |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Low risk | Docs, Internal Wiki | docs-edit | Self-service | Instant | Persistent (attached to employment) |
| Medium risk | Staging CI, Dev DB | staging-deploy | Manager | 48 business hours | 90 days (auto-renew) |
| High risk | Production infra, Billing | prod-admin | Manager + Security | 3 business days | 7 days (explicit extension only) |

6) Exception and Emergency Access

sections.section_path: Entitlements And Purchase Pathways Playbook 2030
sections.heading: Entitlements And Purchase Pathways Playbook 2030
sections.content:
- Standard change: pre-approved, repeatable changes (e.g., routine OS patching via controlled pipeline). Requires change ticket and notification to SRE runbook subscribers.
- Normal change: requires Change Review Board (CRB) approval for higher impact (planned releases that affect SLAs). CRB meets twice weekly.
- Emergency change: immediate fixes that must follow the emergency roll-forward checklist and be retroactively documented in the change ticket.

Change windows and freezes:

- Quarterly freeze: last two business days of each quarter are freeze windows for major releases unless exception approved by CTO and SRE lead.
- High-risk releases: require canary rollout and 30% traffic validation for 24 hours before full rollout.

Change request minimum content (ticket):

1. Change owner and contact
2. Rollout and rollback plan with automation steps
3. Expected impact and post-deploy validation steps
4. Backout criteria and timeline
5. Stakeholder notification list

SLOs and audit

- All normal changes must have an associated ticket and be auditable for 12 months.
- Emergency changes must be documented within 48 hours.

Data management and classification
--------------------------------
Classification levels:

- Public: content intended for public consumption.
- Internal: operational information not intended for external distribution.
- Confidential: employee, business, or customer information that requires access controls.
- Restricted: regulated or highly sensitive data (PII, payment data, health data) that requires encryption at rest and in transit, strict access controls, and audit logging.

Handling rules (summary):

- Confidential & Restricted: store only in approved systems (Redwood Console vaults, encrypted S3 with KMS). No vendor transfer without security and legal sign-off.
- Data retention: default retention for logs is 90 days; for customer-facing telemetry retention follows contractual obligations.
- Data deletion: use Data Erasure Request form and verify via automated deletion job.

Procurement and expenses
------------------------
Purchase approval thresholds (effective):

| Amount (USD) | Approvals required | Notes |
|--------------|-------------------|-------|
| < 2,500 | Manager | Auto-approval in VendorHub if budget tag present |
| 2,500 – 50,000 | Manager + Finance | Finance checks budget and tax classification |
| > 50,000 | Manager + Finance + Procurement + Legal | Requires exec sponsor and procurement intake form |

Procurement steps (numbered):

1. Create a request in VendorHub including business justification, vendor name, SOW/quote, and budget tag.
2. Attach vendor compliance docs (SOC2, ISO, insurance certificate) when available.
3. Finance validates budgets and tax treatment within 3 business days.
4. Procurement routes to Legal for >50k or non-standard T&Cs.
5. Once approved, Procurement issues purchase order and coordinates supplier setup.

Expense reimbursement:

- Use ExpenseFlow, attach receipts within 30 days of expense. Per diem caps: domestic $150/day, international $250/day unless pre-approved. Card use: corporate cards are preferred for travel; personal card reimbursements require manager approval.

Team — pls review Trident redlines (attached). Need positions + proposed counter language today.

Top risk flags / where we likely need to counter:
A) Data residency / “no processing outside US”

- We can generally commit to processing in the customer-selected region for Private/VPC, but need to be careful about support access, telemetry, and backups. We should avoid an absolute “no bytes ever leave US” statement.
- Ask: Naomi/Aisha — what can we safely say re: support systems and subprocessors? Any standard language for “support may access from outside but data remains in-region” vs “support access limited to US persons” etc.

B) Retention / deletion

- They want 0-day retention by default + deletion within 24 hours.
- Need to align with product realities: request logs / audit logs retention is configurable; but 0-day might break ops/troubleshooting.

C) Audit logs / 7-year retention + SIEM export requirement

- We can offer export hooks (customer-controlled destination) + sample schema, but 7-year retention in our systems is a commercial/compliance add-on question and probably “customer retains in their SIEM” rather than us.

sections.content:
Summary

This ADR defines how Redwood Hosted assigns requests to **baseline** vs **canary** cohorts during a hosted canary rollout, and how the configured canary percentage is enforced across regions. The decision prioritizes:

- Deterministic, reproducible cohort assignment (especially across retries)
- Sticky behavior when customers provide stable identifiers
- Minimal coordination/state across regions and data planes
- Observability clarity when effective serving differs from intended cohort

sections.content:
- Initial intake: vendor submitted via VendorHub, 1 business day acknowledgement.
- Risk assessment: Security performs questionnaire review; expect 5-7 business days for standard vendors, 15-20 days for those handling Restricted data.
- Contracting: Legal drafts/negotiates terms; standard NDA/SOW templates for low-risk vendors. Time: 5–15 business days depending on terms.
- Procurement & finance: vendor setup (W-9/COI), tax classification, payment terms.

Minimum vendor requirements by risk tier:

- Low risk (no data access): PO, standard SOE, vendor contact, invoice cadence.
- Medium risk (limited data access): PO, signed DPA, security questionnaire, SOC2 Type II preferred.
- High risk (customer data or privileged infra access): PO, DPA, SOC2 Type II or penetration test report, system access plan, contractual breach notification clause, indemnity terms.

Offboarding and termination:

- Termination checklist: revoke credentials, recover assets, enforce data return/deletion, final invoice reconciliation, and a post-termination confirmation from vendor. Procurement must retain termination evidence for 7 years.

Travel policy (high level)
-------------------------

Booking: Use Travel Portal (linked from Redwood Console). Lowest reasonable fare policy applies for economy class. Business class requires exec-level pre-approval for travel over 8 hours.

Approvals: Manager approves travel requests in Travel Portal. International travel must include security and people-ops notification if travel is to high-risk countries listed by People Ops.

Per diems and expenses: See ExpenseFlow caps. Receipts required for all items >$25.

Safety and incident reporting:

- In case of an incident while traveling, contact People Ops emergency line and Security: security@redwood.com. All incidents must be reported within 24 hours.

Templates and forms (where to find)
----------------------------------

- Procurement intake form: VendorHub > New Request > Procurement Intake (use template 'Procurement-Intake-v2').
- Data Erasure Request: Redwood Console > Data Requests.

sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Burn-rate alerting > Paging vs ticketing
sections.content:
Paging vs ticketing

**Paging alerts (customer-impacting / requires oncall response):**

- **Fast burn:** burn rate >= **14x** over **1h** AND burn rate >= **6x** over **6h**
  - Interpretation: likely to exhaust error budget within ~2.1 days if sustained.

**Ticket alerts (investigate during business hours):**

- **Slow burn:** burn rate >= **3x** over **24h**
  - Interpretation: will exhaust error budget within ~10 days if sustained.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Context / problem
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Context / problem
sections.content:
Context / problem

Hosted canary rollouts require percentage-based traffic splitting on a Hosted route (e.g., 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%) while maintaining:

- Consistent cohorting so a given end user/conversation does not “flip” unpredictably
- Correctness under retries, streaming, and regional failover
- Clear metrics for baseline vs canary cohorts (including when the system must fall back)

Constraints:

- Data plane enforcement must be fast and operate without a central “assignment service.”
- Region routing and model fallback already exist; cohorting must compose cleanly.
- Customers may or may not provide stable end-user identifiers.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 6) Fallback behavior and “effective cohort” telemetry
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 6) Fallback behavior and “effective cohort” telemetry
sections.content:
6) Fallback behavior and “effective cohort” telemetry

If the intended cohort target cannot be served (e.g., canary model unavailable in a region, or hard failure triggers fallback), the system may serve from an alternate target.

Definitions:

- **intended_cohort:** baseline | canary (result of cohort function)
- **effective_target:** the model/version/config actually used after fallback
- **effective_cohort:** baseline | canary, derived from `effective_target` mapping

Telemetry requirements (must be emitted on every request):

- `rollout_id` (when applicable)
- `intended_cohort` (baseline/canary)
- `effective_cohort` (baseline/canary)
- `fallback_reason` (empty or one of: canary_unavailable, canary_error, capacity, policy_denied, region_failover, other)

Customer-facing metrics views:

- Default charts compare **effective_cohort** baseline vs canary (what was actually served).
- Secondary diagnostics show intended vs effective mismatch counts (to detect “phantom canary”).

Safety rule:

- If the rollout is in a state requiring canary availability guarantees (e.g., higher steps), policy may deny progressing if `canary_unavailable` is non-zero in any eligible region for a configured lookback window (guardrail; tracked separately).

Elaine — thank you. We reviewed and prepared a set of counters that we believe addresses Trident’s core requirements for a Private (VPC) deployment while staying aligned with our operational and security commitments.

Attached: Redwood_Proposed_DPA_SLA_Counters_Trident_2025-05-20.docx

High-level summary of key positions:
1) Data residency / processing location

- For a Private (VPC) deployment, we can commit that Customer Content (e.g., prompts and outputs) will be processed and stored within the agreed deployment region/VPC.
- We proposed edits to avoid an absolute prohibition that could unintentionally restrict necessary support and security operations. We included language that any administrative access is controlled, limited, and auditable.

2) Retention / deletion

- We proposed separating (a) retention of Customer Content from (b) retention of operational/audit logs.
- We can support configurable retention settings consistent with the Private deployment architecture. We countered the “0-day retention by default” and “24-hour deletion” requirements with a more operationally feasible deletion standard while still meeting the underlying objective (minimizing retention of customer content).

3) Audit logs / SIEM export / 7-year retention

- We can support audit logging and export so Trident can ingest logs into its SIEM and retain them for 7 years (or longer) under Trident’s control.
- We proposed edits so long-term retention is satisfied via export/retention in Trident systems, rather than requiring Redwood to retain logs for 7 years.

4) Security incident notice

- We proposed notification “without undue delay” and within a defined window following confirmation of a Security Incident affecting Customer Data.

5) Liability and SLA credits

- We proposed standard positions on liability and a bounded service credit structure.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 2) Cohort key selection rules (stickiness)
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 2) Cohort key selection rules (stickiness)
sections.content:
2) Cohort key selection rules (stickiness)

The data plane selects `cohort_key` using the following precedence order:

1. **Explicit Cohort Key header (preferred):**
   - `X-Redwood-Cohort-Key` (customer-provided stable identifier)
   - Recommended values: end_user_id, account_id, conversation_id, or a stable hash thereof

2. **Idempotency key (recommended for retries/streaming reconnects):**
   - `Idempotency-Key` (if present)
   - Intended to remain identical across client retries and stream reconnect attempts

3. **Request ID (best-effort fallback):**
   - `X-Request-Id` (if present)
   - If generated by Redwood, it is unique per attempt and does **not** provide end-user stickiness; it only makes repeated internal handling of the same request deterministic.

4. **Non-sticky fallback (last resort):**
   - A per-request generated UUID (ensures correct aggregate percentage but no per-user stickiness)

Console/Docs requirements:

- Console wizard and docs MUST recommend using `X-Redwood-Cohort-Key` or `Idempotency-Key` for best results.
- Console must warn when a customer’s observed request mix suggests low stickiness (optional; informational).

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 3) Where cohorting is enforced
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 3) Where cohorting is enforced
sections.content:
3) Where cohorting is enforced

Cohorting and split enforcement occur in the **Smart Routing / data plane** after route resolution and policy checks, and before final model selection.

Order (simplified):

1. Authenticate request / resolve tenant + route
2. Evaluate policy eligibility for rollout (RBAC, guardrails, rollout state)
3. Select region per existing routing policies (latency/capacity/affinity)
4. **Compute cohort (baseline/canary) in the chosen region’s data plane**
5. Select model version/config for the cohort
6. Apply existing fallback policies if the chosen target is unavailable

sections.section_path: Metering To Invoice Reconciliation Playbook > Thresholds and SLOs (default) > Correctness/drift
sections.heading: Metering To Invoice Reconciliation Playbook > Thresholds and SLOs (default) > Correctness/drift
sections.content:
Correctness/drift

All drift thresholds are computed at the reconciliation grain.

- **Daily drift (Hosted API tokens):** absolute drift ≤ **0.25%** AND ≤ **$250** per account-day
- **Weekly drift:** absolute drift ≤ **0.10%** AND ≤ **$500** per account-week
- **Dedicated GPU-seconds:** absolute drift ≤ **0.20%** AND ≤ **$500** per account-day

sections.section_path: Billing Meter Spec Hosted Api Tokens And Requests > 7. Token metering rules > 7.5 Cache-hit attribution and billed tokens
sections.heading: Billing Meter Spec Hosted Api Tokens And Requests > 7. Token metering rules > 7.5 Cache-hit attribution and billed tokens
sections.content:
7.5 Cache-hit attribution and billed tokens

Hosted API may apply caching at different layers:

- Prefix/KV cache (compute reduction, same semantic output generation)
- Response cache (replay exact output)

Metering requirements:

- Record `cache_hit = true/false` and `cache_type` (optional: `kv_prefix`, `response`, `other`).
- Record `raw_tokens` as normal.
- Record `billed_tokens` according to active pricing plan policy.

Current billing policy (default unless overridden in plan):

- Cache hits do **not** change `billed_tokens` (billed remains aligned to customer-visible usage). Cache attribution is used for margin analysis and pricing experiments.

If a future plan bills cache hits differently, that plan must:

- Explicitly define `cache_billing_policy` (e.g., `full`, `discounted`, `free_prompt`, etc.)
- Expose that policy in contract/order form language as required by Legal
- Be introduced only with meter_version bump and shadow compare (§11)

sections.content:
3) “Usage Report” / “Usage API”

**Usage Report** means Redwood’s reported usage as displayed in the Console, invoice detail, or usage export/API. Contract language should clarify which report is authoritative for billing.

Internal preference:

- For contracts: define that **Redwood’s invoice and supporting usage report** is the authoritative basis for fees, subject to the dispute process.

sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Implementation notes (non-normative)
sections.content:
Implementation notes (non-normative)

- Data plane should compute cohort as early as possible after route resolution, but after any bypass/policy deny checks.
- Keep the hash implementation identical across languages (gateway, edge proxies, and routing services). Add a golden test vector suite.
- Add integration tests to validate:
  - Stable assignment across retries with same idempotency key
  - Step increases are monotonic superset of canary population
  - Fallback produces intended/effective mismatch telemetry

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Detailed specification > Exclusions / bypass
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Detailed specification > Exclusions / bypass
sections.content:
Exclusions / bypass

Certain traffic must not participate in rollouts:

- Health checks, internal synthetic probes, and system-to-system calls used for SLO verification.

Mechanism:

- Internal callers set `X-Redwood-Bypass-Rollout: true` (restricted to Redwood internal auth).
- If bypassed, cohorting is skipped and the baseline target is selected; telemetry marks `rollout_bypassed=true`.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Detailed specification > Cohort key normalization
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Detailed specification > Cohort key normalization
sections.content:
Detailed specification

Cohort key normalization

To avoid accidental cohort churn:

- Use the cohort key exactly as received (no trimming/case folding), except:
  - Reject keys longer than **256 bytes** (return validation error: `cohort_key_too_long`)
  - Reject keys containing NUL bytes
- Do not log raw cohort keys (treat as potentially sensitive). If needed for debugging, log a truncated hash.

sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language)
sections.content:

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 4) How configured percentages apply across regions
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 4) How configured percentages apply across regions
sections.content:
4) How configured percentages apply across regions

Configured canary percentage is enforced **independently per region**, using the same deterministic function.

Meaning:

- The system does **not** attempt to maintain an exact global canary percentage across all regions combined.
- Each region will converge to the configured percentage for traffic that is routed to that region.

Rationale:

- Avoids cross-region coordination/state and reduces blast radius.
- Aligns canary metrics to the region where traffic was actually served.
- Prevents “global percentage drift” caused by sudden regional routing shifts.

Known consequence:

- If a single end user is routed to different regions on different requests (e.g., due to region failover or customer not using region affinity), they may land in different cohorts because the cohorting is evaluated after region selection and because the available model set can differ by region.

Mitigation:

- Customers who require strict consistency should use region pinning/affinity (where supported) and provide a stable `X-Redwood-Cohort-Key`.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 1) Deterministic cohorting function
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 1) Deterministic cohorting function
sections.content:
Decision

1) Deterministic cohorting function

Cohort assignment is computed as a pure function:
**cohort = f(route_id, rollout_id, cohort_key)**
Where:

- `route_id` is the canonical Hosted route identifier
- `rollout_id` is the rollout instance identifier (changes per rollout)
- `cohort_key` is a stable string chosen per request (see selection rules below)

Implementation:

- Hash function: **xxHash64** (or equivalent stable 64-bit non-cryptographic hash) over UTF-8 bytes
- Input format (must be stable and unambiguous):
  - `"v1|" + route_id + "|" + rollout_id + "|" + cohort_key`
- Convert hash → bucket:
  - `bucket = hash64 % 10000` (0–9999)
- Compare to configured canary percentage:
  - `is_canary = bucket < (canary_percent * 100)`
  - Example: 5% → threshold 500

Rationale:

- Pure function = deterministic across restarts, regions, and retries (given same `cohort_key`).
- 10,000 buckets provides 0.01% granularity while remaining simple.
- Including `rollout_id` avoids “stickiness” across separate rollouts (a new rollout should re-sample cohorts).

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Saturation requirement (practical interpretation)
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Saturation requirement (practical interpretation)
sections.content:
Saturation requirement (practical interpretation)

This SLO is designed to answer: “When the customer is **trying** to use their Dedicated capacity, do we deliver the committed throughput?”

Therefore, compliance reporting only considers periods where the deployment is **meaningfully loaded**.

We define “meaningfully loaded” for a window as:

- `eligible_generation_wall_time_seconds >= 120` seconds within the 5-minute window

If a window does not meet the load threshold, it is treated as **insufficient demand** and excluded from compliance (removed from total). This prevents underutilized deployments from producing misleading ‘low throughput’ windows.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Consequences > Negative / tradeoffs
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Consequences > Negative / tradeoffs
sections.content:
Negative / tradeoffs

- Stickiness is only as good as the provided key; without it, customer experience may vary.
- Regional independence means some users may move cohorts if they move regions.
- Must be careful with metric cardinality (rollout_id + cohort tags); see telemetry guidelines.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Detailed specification > Percent precision and step changes
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Detailed specification > Percent precision and step changes
sections.content:
Percent precision and step changes

- Percent is stored as a decimal with two decimal places (0.00–100.00).
- Changing percent changes the threshold; users move cohorts deterministically based on their bucket.
- This behavior is desired: when going from 5%→25%, the additional 20% is a deterministic superset.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Options considered > Option B: Central assignment service (store user→cohort mappings)
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Options considered > Option B: Central assignment service (store user→cohort mappings)
sections.content:
Option B: Central assignment service (store user→cohort mappings)

- Pros: strong stickiness; globally consistent
- Cons: adds new stateful service; latency and availability risks; heavy operational overhead; complicated privacy considerations
- Rejected for GA.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 5) Handling retries, streaming, and internal re-attempts > Streaming
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Decision > 5) Handling retries, streaming, and internal re-attempts > Streaming
sections.content:
Streaming

- Streaming responses are treated as a single request attempt. Cohort is computed at stream start.
- If a client reconnects and expects consistent behavior, it must reuse `Idempotency-Key` (and ideally `X-Redwood-Cohort-Key`).

sections.heading: 2026 01 16 Gcp Marketplace Onboarding And Billing Review
sections.content:
[06:55] Miguel Alvarez: Dedicated capacity tends to fit better as subscription / contract. Usage metering for “gpu hours” works, but you need to align it with what you’re actually providing. If it’s truly reserved, then a monthly subscription fee is clearer. If there’s burst/overage, you can meter overage separately.

[07:16] Nadia Rahman: We can do either. Internally we track reserved pool size and then tokens anyway, but the contract is the key. If you recommend subscription for reserved, then our metering is mostly for overage.

[07:29] Priya Shah: From a procurement standpoint, enterprise buyers usually prefer a predictable subscription line item. Then usage-based Hosted is more PLG.

[07:41] Stephanie Nguyen: That matches what we’re seeing. One thing we’re worried about: we want three clear “paths” in the listing—Hosted, Dedicated, Private. But under the hood GCP constructs are not always “three products.” It’s one listing with plans, right?

[07:57] Priya Shah: Exactly. You typically have one product listing and multiple plans. You can describe the three modes in the copy, but technically it’s one product with pricing plans.

[08:12] Ben Carter: On the onboarding, would you expect different landing pages for different plans? Like, if someone buys Private, they shouldn’t be dropped into “create API key and call the hosted endpoint” because their next step is networking and deployment.

[08:26] Anika Desai: That’s a good point. Ideally yes: after entitlement, route them to the appropriate next steps. But you can also have a general landing page that asks “what did you purchase?” or reads the plan from the entitlement.

[08:43] Cole Summers: Reading the plan from entitlement is doable if the entitlement includes plan name. We just need to be careful with plan rename.

[08:52] Miguel Alvarez: Plan rename is okay if you keep the underlying plan ID stable. Don’t key logic off display name.

[09:01] Chris Osei: Noted. We’ll key off ID.

[09:05] Stephanie Nguyen: Let’s talk about reviewer expectations on the metering payload. Miguel, can you share what they check?

[09:14] Miguel Alvarez: Sure. They’ll check: (1) you’re using the correct API endpoints, (2) the consumerId or entitlement is valid, (3) the dimension is a valid one configured in your offer, (4) the quantity is non-negative and within reason, (5) timestamps are sane (not future by a day), (6) idempotency—you don’t double bill on retry.

[09:40] Nadia Rahman: On idempotency: we have an internal “usage_event_id” and we can keep a ledger. If we retry, we send the same event id. Is that a pattern you like to see?

[09:52] Miguel Alvarez: Yes. Exactly. Store the request ID and mark it as sent. Most of the “billing mismatch” issues are duplicate sends during outages.

[10:05] Ben Carter: Do you have any advice on how to validate end-to-end that metering is going to show up for the customer? Like, in AWS we can see it in the buyer account pretty quickly.

sections.section_path: Usage Meter Audit 2026 02 Working Notes
sections.heading: Usage Meter Audit 2026 02 Working Notes
sections.content:
- Largest deltas concentrated in streaming + retry-heavy workloads.
- Embeddings batched fix creates visible downshift in billed units for affected endpoints (expected).
- Some “unexpected” upshifts tied to region dimension fill-in (previously dropped rows now counted).

Action items

- Aisha: add dashboard annotation when “dimension fill” fixes cause apparent billing increase (so Finance understands expected behavior).
- Emily: list accounts needing proactive comms if billed totals change materially post-fix (coordinate with Support/Sales).

Daily sanity checks we want (Finance POV)
(These are what we keep asking for; Eng is building dashboard/job + alerts)

- Drift: |sum(usage_events billed_tokens) - sum(billing_ledger billed_tokens)| / ledger <= threshold
- Duplicate usage events rate (by dedupe key)
- Null rate for required dimensions: account_id, model, region, endpoint, request_id/idempotency_key
- Freshness: P95 event available in recon export within X minutes; P99 within Y hours
- “Dropped rows” count in aggregation pipeline (rows failing schema validation)

Draft thresholds (proposed — needs PM-1842 sign-off)

- Drift paging: >1.0% for any top-20 account daily OR >0.3% platform-wide daily
- Duplicate rate paging: >0.05% daily
- Freshness paging: P99 > 6 hours
- Null required dims paging: >0.1% for any required dim

Month-end close policy notes (WIP)
Freeze window proposal

- Close month M at M+3 calendar days 23:59 UTC for usage event ingestion into ledger.
- Late events after freeze: record as “late adjustments” and post to next month unless material + approved for adjustment.

Need to document

- Evidence retained: snapshot of ledger totals, reconciliation export query outputs, variance explanations, approvals.
- Audit trail for meter changes: PR link + shadow billing diff report + Finance sign-off + effective date.

Customer-facing / legal language questions (capturing for Legal)

- Token definition: which tokenizer/version; what counts as prompt vs completion; tool call tokens.
- Retries: “We do not charge additional tokens for server-side retries/fallback” (if true) vs “we charge for tokens generated” (if partials count).
- Caching: how prefix cache reduces billed prompt tokens; whether cache-hit depends on exact match; transparency in reporting.
- Dispute window: timeframe and required evidence (usage export as source? invoice ledger as source?)
- Audit logs: ability to provide per-request usage records under NDA?

- We should sample at least 15 invoices: 5 self-serve, 5 sales-led, 5 dedicated.
- Priority: accounts with streaming >50% and high retry rate.

- Customers pushing hard on “token counting fairness” and “no double charge for retries.”
- Michael: prefer explicit definitions + examples; avoid promising perfect alignment with third-party tokenizers if we can’t guarantee.

sections.content:
Appendix: example exhibit (usage definitions)

Use only when procurement requires a detailed exhibit; keep it concise.

**Exhibit X — Usage Definitions (Example)**

- “Billed Tokens” means the token quantity reported by Redwood for billing, which may account for caching adjustments and promotional inclusions, as reflected in Redwood’s usage report.
- “Idempotency Key” means a unique identifier provided by Customer to allow safe retries without duplicate logical charges.

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings) > 1) “Token”
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings) > 1) “Token”
sections.content:
1) “Token”

**Token** means a discrete unit of text as processed by the applicable model’s tokenization scheme. Tokenization is model-dependent.

Important internal positions:

- Token counts are **model-specific** and may differ between models and versions.
- For chat-style endpoints, token counts may include system/developer messages, tool call payloads, and structured output formatting as applicable.
- We support (and prefer to contract around) **billed tokens** as the invoicing unit, rather than raw “input + output tokens,” because billed tokens reflects caching/discounting rules.

Recommended terminology:

- **Input Tokens / Prompt Tokens**: tokens attributable to the request context provided by the customer.
- **Output Tokens / Completion Tokens**: tokens generated by the model in response.
- **Billed Tokens**: the token quantity used for billing after applying billing rules (e.g., caching adjustments, promotional discounts, free-tier inclusion), as shown on the invoice and/or usage reports.

[24:16] Chris Osei: I want to make sure we leave with concrete outputs. Cole will send a proposed mapping table and example payloads. Anika and Miguel will send docs and constraints. Ben will share screenshots/wireframes.

[24:31] Stephanie Nguyen: One question: in GCP marketplace, do customers expect to get credits / trial? We offer free credits on our website; does marketplace support that?

[24:41] Priya Shah: Marketplace trials exist in some contexts but not universally. Many partners handle trials outside marketplace or do a low-cost starter plan. If you want a trial, we can discuss, but it may complicate approval.

[24:56] Stephanie Nguyen: We’ll keep it simple for now.

[24:59] Ben Carter: Another thing: we have a dedicated onboarding docs page. Is it okay to link external docs from the listing?

[25:07] Priya Shah: Yes, you can link to documentation. Just make sure it’s stable URLs.

[25:12] Chris Osei: We’re finalizing vanity redirects for marketplace. Okay.

[25:16] (minor audio glitch)

[25:18] Nadia Rahman: Can we ask about time window for metering submissions? Like can we send usage events delayed by a day?

[25:26] Miguel Alvarez: There is a window; don’t send extremely late. A few hours delay is okay. A day is sometimes okay but not ideal. Send as close to real time as possible. Again, I’ll send guidance.

[25:43] Nadia Rahman: Got it.

[25:45] Cole Summers: For retry logic, if API errors, we retry with exponential backoff. If it fails for a long time, we queue. We can cap backlog.

[25:54] Miguel Alvarez: That’s fine. But make sure you don’t exceed the allowed backfill window.

[26:02] Stephanie Nguyen: Okay.

[26:04] Priya Shah: Any other questions from Redwood before we wrap?

[26:09] Stephanie Nguyen: I have one more: procurement question. Some buyers will ask “does buying through marketplace change the support terms / SLAs?” We have dedicated support tiers. Do you see any constraints on what we can say?

[26:23] Priya Shah: You can state support terms clearly. Just avoid promising things you can’t deliver. If there’s a premium SLA, you can make it a plan or an add-on, but it should be consistent.

[26:37] Ben Carter: We’ll align with our support team.

[26:40] Chris Osei: Okay. Let’s do a quick recap and next steps.

[26:45] Chris Osei: Recap:

- Dimension strategy: keep Hosted usage-based with a small set of dimensions (tokens, embeddings), use subscription plans for Dedicated/Private, consider bundled plans for compliance add-ons.
- Use stable IDs, don’t key logic off display names.
- Handle entitlement propagation delays with friendly UI + retry.
- Implement idempotency for metering events and alert on 4xx errors.
- Run staging test: subscribe -> entitlement -> org link -> API key -> sample traffic -> verify metering -> cancellation/plan change.

[27:21] Stephanie Nguyen: And action items: Cole will send draft mapping + payload examples, Ben will send UX screens, Anika/Miguel will send docs on quotas/rounding/validation.

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Purpose
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Purpose
sections.content:
Purpose

This playbook provides Redwood Inference’s approved legal guidance and clause library for **usage-based pricing** across Redwood API (Hosted) and related packaging. It is designed to:

- Ensure **consistent definitions** (tokens, requests, cache hits, retries) across MSAs, Order Forms, pricing pages, and Sales communications.
- Reduce **invoice disputes** by aligning contract language with metering behavior.
- Support **revenue recognition (RevRec)** and audit readiness by defining authoritative sources, dispute windows, and credit/refund mechanics.

This page is **restricted** because it contains clause language and internal positions.

sections.section_path: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Options considered > Option D: Enforce percentage globally across regions
sections.heading: Adr Hosted Rollout Cohorting And Traffic Splitting > Options considered > Option D: Enforce percentage globally across regions
sections.content:
Option D: Enforce percentage globally across regions

- Pros: global percentage invariance
- Cons: requires coordination/state or cross-region sampling; complex under routing shifts
- Rejected for GA. (Can be revisited if we introduce a global routing coordinator.)

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings) > 5) “Retry”
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings) > 5) “Retry”
sections.content:
5) “Retry”

Retry can occur on:

- **Client side** (customer’s SDK/app retries)
- **Server side** (Redwood retries/fallback routing to preserve availability)

Internal positions:

- We aim to bill **once per logical request** where retries are transparently handled under the same idempotency key.
- If the customer does not use idempotency keys and submits duplicate requests, those may be billable.

sections.section_path: Metering To Invoice Reconciliation Playbook > Thresholds and SLOs (default) > Dimension completeness
sections.heading: Metering To Invoice Reconciliation Playbook > Thresholds and SLOs (default) > Dimension completeness
sections.content:
Dimension completeness

- Null rate for required dimensions (account_id, usage_date, product_route, region, model/sku): **< 0.05%**
- Duplicate usage_event_id rate post-dedupe: **< 0.02%**

---

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings) > 4) “Caching” / “Cache Hit”
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings) > 4) “Caching” / “Cache Hit”
sections.content:
4) “Caching” / “Cache Hit”

Caching may reduce compute performed by Redwood. Contract language must avoid obligating Redwood to charge based on compute cost; instead, define how caching affects billed tokens.

Internal position:

- We may apply **cache-hit attribution** to reduce billed usage for eligible cached content, as described in product documentation.
- Caching behavior can change over time as the service is optimized; the contract should permit evolution while maintaining transparency via reports.

sections.section_path: Billing Meter Spec Hosted Api Tokens And Requests > 4. Definitions > 4.3 “Chargeable event time”
sections.heading: Billing Meter Spec Hosted Api Tokens And Requests > 4. Definitions > 4.3 “Chargeable event time”
sections.content:
4.3 “Chargeable event time”

All Hosted API meters roll up by **UTC usage date**, based on `metered_at` (see §10). Export/UI may render in customer timezone, but the ledger uses UTC for close.

---

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Drafting guidance (what to include in usage-based terms) > Required building blocks
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Drafting guidance (what to include in usage-based terms) > Required building blocks
sections.content:
Drafting guidance (what to include in usage-based terms)

Required building blocks

For any Order Form/SOW with usage-based fees, include:
1) Usage unit definition (tokens, embeddings units, requests, GPU-seconds if applicable)
2) Billing measurement and reporting source (invoice + usage report)
3) Caching and retries treatment (at least at a high level)
4) Dispute window + audit mechanics (reasonable; avoids open-ended re-billing risk)
5) Credits/refunds policy (when available; how applied)
6) Change management notice (especially if customer requests strict metering invariants)

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > D. Tool/function calling and structured output
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > D. Tool/function calling and structured output
sections.content:
D. Tool/function calling and structured output

**Approved clause (standard):**
“Where the service supports tool/function calling or structured output, tokens attributable to tool call inputs/outputs and associated formatting may be included in token usage as reported by Redwood.”

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > I. Credits and refunds (usage-based)
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > I. Credits and refunds (usage-based)
sections.content:
I. Credits and refunds (usage-based)

**Approved clause (standard):**
“Credits, if any, are applied to future invoices unless otherwise required by law. Except as expressly provided in the Agreement, fees are non-refundable.”

**Optional add-on (when SLA credits apply):**
“Service credits are Customer’s sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet a service level, and will be calculated and applied as described in the applicable SLA.”

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > E. Caching treatment
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > E. Caching treatment
sections.content:
E. Caching treatment

**Approved clause (standard):**
“Redwood may employ caching and other optimization techniques. Usage reports may distinguish cached and non-cached usage. Redwood may apply billing adjustments (including reduced billed tokens) for eligible cached content as described in Redwood documentation. Optimization techniques may change over time.”

**Alternative clause (customer requests explicit fairness statement):**
“Redwood will not charge more than once for the same logical request submitted with the same idempotency key, and may reduce charges when caching is applied, as reflected in the usage report.”

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings) > 2) “Request”
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings) > 2) “Request”
sections.content:
2) “Request”

A **Request** is an API call that is accepted by Redwood’s service and results in an attempt to process the call (including streaming requests). Do not tie “request” to “successful response” unless Product/Finance explicitly approves.

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > A. Usage unit (Tokens) — baseline clause
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > A. Usage unit (Tokens) — baseline clause
sections.content:
A. Usage unit (Tokens) — baseline clause

**Approved clause (standard):**
“Usage is measured in tokens processed by the applicable model. A token is a unit of text determined by the model’s tokenization scheme. Fees are calculated based on the number of billed tokens reported by Redwood for the applicable billing period. Token counts may vary by model and model version.”

**Negotiation notes:**

- If customer requests a fixed tokenization algorithm, respond that tokenization is model-dependent and tied to the model provider’s implementation.
- If customer requests billing purely on input+output tokens, steer to “billed tokens” and point to reporting transparency.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Error budget policy (operational gates) > Policy thresholds (rolling 30-day)
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Error budget policy (operational gates) > Policy thresholds (rolling 30-day)
sections.content:
Policy thresholds (rolling 30-day)

- **Healthy:** >= 70% error budget remaining
  - Normal change velocity.
- **Watch:** 30–70% error budget remaining
  - Requires SRE review for changes that can impact serving performance (runtime upgrades, kernel toggles, routing policy changes).
- **At risk:** < 30% error budget remaining
  - Freeze performance-risky changes for affected tier/pool unless explicitly approved by SRE lead (Rafael Mendes) and Infra lead (Irene Choi).
- **Exhausted:** SLO below target
  - Treat as an incident for Dedicated customers; engage CS per escalation playbook; credits/remedies handled per commercial terms.

sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Canonical SLI and SLO > Requests/sec as a secondary metric
sections.content:
Requests/sec as a secondary metric

Requests/sec may be used for:

- Non-generative routes where token accounting is not meaningful (rare in Dedicated scope), or
- As an internal diagnostic view (e.g., “QPS at steady state”) alongside tokens/sec.

If requests/sec is used, it is explicitly labeled as a **non-canonical** SLI and must not be substituted for compliance without SRE sign-off.

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > F. Retries and idempotency
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > F. Retries and idempotency
sections.content:
F. Retries and idempotency

**Approved clause (standard):**
“Customer is responsible for implementing idempotency keys for retryable requests. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to avoid duplicate billing for server-side retries performed under the same logical request identifier. Customer-submitted duplicate requests may be billable.”

**Negotiation notes:**

- Do not guarantee “no double billing ever.” Instead: “commercially reasonable efforts” + dispute process.

**Approved clause (standard):**

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Purpose
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Purpose
sections.content:
Purpose

This page defines the canonical Service Level Objective (SLO) for **Dedicated throughput** at Redwood Inference, including:

- SLI and metric semantics (tokens/sec as canonical; when requests/sec is used)
- Measurement windows and aggregation
- Exclusions and “not counted” conditions
- Burn-rate alerting and error budget policy
- Reporting requirements and ownership

This is the formal reference used by SRE, Observability, Infra/Fleet, and Product when implementing dashboards, alerts, incident classification, and customer-facing reporting.

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Internal operational guardrails (contracting) > Customer communications
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Internal operational guardrails (contracting) > Customer communications
sections.content:
Customer communications

If contract or procurement asks for a customer-facing explanation:

- Sales should use the approved FAQ language (see Sales Enablement page) and avoid promising exact token parity or “never bill on retries.”

sections.section_path: Sup 18421 Enterprise 429 Spike After Priority Routing Rollout > Initial support response (guidance provided)
sections.heading: Sup 18421 Enterprise 429 Spike After Priority Routing Rollout > Initial support response (guidance provided)
sections.content:
Initial support response (guidance provided)

- Confirmed that the new system returns distinct reason codes and customers should key their retry/backoff behavior on:
  - "quota_exceeded" (respect quota windows; reduce steady-state rate)
  - "overload_protection_admission" (transient overload; respect Retry-After; use exponential backoff + jitter)
- Recommended changes:
  - Use exponential backoff with full jitter; cap concurrency; do not retry immediately.
  - Honor Retry-After; treat 429 as a signal to shed load client-side.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Scope > Applies to
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Scope > Applies to
sections.content:
Scope

Applies to

- **Dedicated deployments** (hosted in Redwood-managed infrastructure) with a **committed throughput floor** recorded in control plane configuration.
- Deployments where a customer has:
  - A pinned **model family + major version** (e.g., `llama-3.x`, `mistral-large.x`) and
  - A configured **max context length** within the supported range for the purchased hardware shape.

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Redlines: common asks and recommended responses > 2) “Do not charge for retries / failed requests.”
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Redlines: common asks and recommended responses > 2) “Do not charge for retries / failed requests.”
sections.content:
2) “Do not charge for retries / failed requests.”

**Position:** If compute is performed, some usage may be reported.
**Response:** Use idempotency + commercially reasonable efforts clause. Offer a credits mechanism for verified platform-caused duplicate charges.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Exclusions (non-counted windows/requests) > Edge-case review (must be documented)
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Exclusions (non-counted windows/requests) > Edge-case review (must be documented)
sections.content:
Edge-case review (must be documented)

If a customer workload has atypical characteristics (e.g., extremely long contexts, highly skewed token distributions, tool-calling patterns with minimal output), the account team must request an SRE review to confirm:

- The correct committed floor unit (tokens/sec vs alternative) and
- The correct eligibility and saturation guidance.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Reporting > Customer-facing reporting (when applicable)
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Reporting > Customer-facing reporting (when applicable)
sections.content:
Customer-facing reporting (when applicable)

- Provide a monthly compliance summary upon request for Plus/Premium tiers.
- Reports must:
  - State the committed throughput floor
  - State the achieved compliance (% good windows)
  - List excluded windows with category and timestamps (maintenance, warm-up)
  - Include a short explanation of the “insufficient demand” exclusion

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Measurement semantics > Streaming token accounting
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Measurement semantics > Streaming token accounting
sections.content:
Streaming token accounting

For streaming responses:

- Output tokens are counted when emitted by the runtime, attributed to the originating request.
- We de-duplicate token counters to avoid double counting caused by stream chunk retries.

Operational note: streaming accounting semantics were corrected in **PR-19422** (“Fix throughput metric double counting streaming”). Any backfills or comparisons across that boundary must annotate the change.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Canonical SLI and SLO > Canonical throughput metric (SLI)
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Canonical SLI and SLO > Canonical throughput metric (SLI)
sections.content:
Canonical SLI and SLO

Canonical throughput metric (SLI)

**SLI name:** Dedicated Throughput Floor Attainment
**SLI definition (per deployment):**
For each `deployment_id`, compute the fraction of eligible 5-minute windows in which the **observed output token rate** meets or exceeds the committed floor.

A 5-minute window is considered **good** if:

- `observed_tps(deployment_id, window) >= committed_tps(deployment_id) * 1.00`

A window is **bad** if:

- `observed_tps(deployment_id, window) < committed_tps(deployment_id) * 1.00`

**Why tokens/sec:** Token throughput is the most stable cross-model, cross-request indicator for generation routes and aligns with customer-perceived capacity for streaming/chat.

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings)
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Definitions (approved internal meanings)
sections.content:
Definitions (approved internal meanings)

The following definitions should be used as the “source definitions” when drafting or redlining contract language. If a customer demands alternate language, follow the escalation path below.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Exclusions (non-counted windows/requests) > Request-level exclusions
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Exclusions (non-counted windows/requests) > Request-level exclusions
sections.content:
Request-level exclusions

The following requests are excluded from both numerator and denominator:

- **Customer-side throttling or pacing** that prevents the deployment from being demand-saturated while measuring throughput (e.g., the customer sends traffic well below the committed floor and attempts to interpret low throughput as non-compliance).
- **Client disconnects / cancellations** before generation completes (where Redwood terminates work early).
- **Invalid requests** or requests that violate documented limits (e.g., context > supported max for the purchased shape, unsupported model version).
- **Customer-enforced caps** that materially reduce achievable throughput, including:
  - Very low `max_tokens` combined with high request overhead patterns (evaluated case-by-case; see “edge-case review” below)
  - Customer-set concurrency limits below recommended saturation settings

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Redlines: common asks and recommended responses > 5) “Audit rights to inspect raw logs.”
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Redlines: common asks and recommended responses > 5) “Audit rights to inspect raw logs.”
sections.content:
5) “Audit rights to inspect raw logs.”

**Position:** No direct customer access to raw multi-tenant logs.
**Response:** Provide usage exports, reconciliation support, and audit reports as appropriate; reference access-controls policy.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Measurement semantics > Observed throughput calculation (tokens/sec)
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Measurement semantics > Observed throughput calculation (tokens/sec)
sections.content:
Observed throughput calculation (tokens/sec)

For each deployment and 5-minute window:

- `observed_tps = eligible_output_tokens / eligible_generation_wall_time_seconds`

Where:

- **eligible_output_tokens** counts output tokens generated for eligible requests whose generation occurs within the window.
- **eligible_generation_wall_time_seconds** is the sum of per-request generation durations for eligible requests, measured at Redwood’s gateway/runtime boundary.

Notes:

- We use **wall time spent generating** rather than total window duration to avoid penalizing low-utilization periods.
- This SLO measures our ability to serve when the customer is asking for capacity, not whether the customer sends enough traffic to saturate the deployment.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Burn-rate alerting > Alert routing
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Burn-rate alerting > Alert routing
sections.content:
Alert routing

- Page: `#eng-oncall` and oncall rotation “SRE - Inference Platform”
- Auto-attach runbook link: “Dedicated Throughput SLO Escalation”
- Auto-include fields: `deployment_id`, `customer_name` (if available), `tier`, `region`, current `observed_tps`, `committed_tps`, top rejection reasons, saturation signals

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Scope > Does not apply to
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Scope > Does not apply to
sections.content:
Does not apply to

- Shared/Hosted API (non-dedicated) traffic
- Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments (separate SLOs)

sections.heading: Hosted Api Slos Enterprise Route Tiers > Operational guidance > Change management

Change management

Changes that affect enterprise SLOs require:

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Measurement semantics > Batching and caching
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Measurement semantics > Batching and caching
sections.content:
Batching and caching

- Continuous batching and prefix/KV caching are treated as implementation details and are inherently included in observed throughput.
- Customers may see throughput increases due to caching; this does not change the committed floor.
- SLO compliance is evaluated on Redwood-side metered tokens/time, not customer-side client timers.

sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Clause library (approved language) > C. Streaming responses — how to describe
sections.content:
C. Streaming responses — how to describe

**Approved clause (standard):**
“For streaming responses, usage is measured based on tokens processed and reported by Redwood for the request. If a streaming connection is interrupted, Redwood may report usage for tokens processed up to the point of interruption.”

sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Canonical SLI and SLO > SLO target
sections.content:
SLO target

**SLO (per deployment):**

- **99.5%** of eligible 5-minute windows over a rolling **30-day** period must be good.

This implies an error budget of **0.5%** of windows per 30 days.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Exclusions (non-counted windows/requests)
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > Exclusions (non-counted windows/requests)
sections.content:
Exclusions (non-counted windows/requests)

Exclusions exist to avoid situations where the throughput floor is not meaningful, is externally constrained, or is not under Redwood’s control.

sections.section_path: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Internal operational guardrails (contracting) > Backfills and corrections
sections.heading: Usage Based Pricing Legal Terms Playbook > Internal operational guardrails (contracting) > Backfills and corrections
sections.content:
Backfills and corrections

If Redwood discovers a metering bug:

- Default approach is **forward-looking fixes** with audit trail.
- Retroactive invoice changes require Finance + Legal approval.

sections.section_path: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > SLO evaluation logic (reference)
sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Definition > SLO evaluation logic (reference)
sections.content:
SLO evaluation logic (reference)

For each deployment_id and 5-minute window:
1) Compute eligible tokens and eligible generation seconds.
2) If `eligible_generation_seconds < 120`, mark window as **excluded_insufficient_demand**.
3) Else compute `observed_tps = tokens / seconds`.
4) Window is good if `observed_tps >= committed_tps`.
The rolling SLO is:

- `good_windows / eligible_windows >= 0.995` over 30 days.

sections.section_path: Billing Meter Spec Hosted Api Tokens And Requests > 7. Token metering rules > 7.4 Billed tokens (billed_tokens)
sections.heading: Billing Meter Spec Hosted Api Tokens And Requests > 7. Token metering rules > 7.4 Billed tokens (billed_tokens)
sections.content:
7.4 Billed tokens (billed_tokens)

`billed_tokens` is the default basis for charging and is computed as:

**billed_tokens = billed_prompt_tokens + billed_completion_tokens**

Unless otherwise specified by pricing policy, the default is:

- `billed_prompt_tokens = prompt_tokens`
- `billed_completion_tokens = completion_tokens`

Billing behavior by outcome:

- **Successful 2xx:** bill billed_tokens per above.
- **Client disconnect during streaming:** bill tokens actually generated and sent prior to disconnect (no future/estimated tokens). Request is billable if at least one token was streamed OR if prompt processing completed and policy bills prompt tokens (current policy: bill prompt tokens if the model began execution; see §7.6).
- **Server error after tokens produced:** bill tokens produced (prompt + completion as applicable). Must not bill tokens for attempts that never started execution.

Customer communications guide

sections.content:
2) Confirm the customer is driving enough load

sections.section_path: Adr 008 Key Rotation Strategy Dual Read And Cutover > Decision > 4) Rollback plan
sections.heading: Adr 008 Key Rotation Strategy Dual Read And Cutover > Decision > 4) Rollback plan
sections.content:
4) Rollback plan

Rollback is defined as reverting primary selection and/or reintroducing previous KeyRefs into the allowed decrypt set.

We will support rollback by:

- Keeping the previous primary key enabled and permitted for decrypt for a minimum retention window (default: 30 days Hosted/Dedicated; Private set by customer policy) after cutover.
- Maintaining a fast config toggle to:
  - Set previous KeyRef as primary again, and
  - Re-enable dual-decrypt with both old and new keys.

Rollback triggers include:

- Sustained increase in InvalidCiphertext/BadDecrypt correlated with cutover.
- Unexplained increase in decrypt latency or throttling after switching keys.
- Customer-reported decrypt errors during Private change window.

sections.section_path: Hosted Api Slos Enterprise Route Tiers > Error budgets > Error budget policy (what we do when we burn)
sections.heading: Hosted Api Slos Enterprise Route Tiers > Error budgets > Error budget policy (what we do when we burn)
sections.content:
Error budget policy (what we do when we burn)

**Enterprise (Protected) routes**

- If burn is elevated, the default stance is **protect SLOs over throughput**.
- Allowed mitigations (in priority order):
  1) Tighten best-effort admission control thresholds (shed earlier)
  2) Temporarily reduce best-effort burst allowances
  3) Increase enterprise reserved capacity / pool weights (if available)
  4) Enable guarded fallback policies where contractually allowed
  5) As last resort: temporary enterprise throttling with exec/on-call approval and proactive comms

**Best-effort routes**

- Best-effort can be shed under pressure; we do not page purely on best-effort 429 shedding.
- If best-effort availability drops due to 5xx (not 429 overload-shed), we investigate as a normal reliability regression.

sections.section_path: Quantization Profiles Customer Docs Plan > Product language and terminology
sections.heading: Quantization Profiles Customer Docs Plan > Product language and terminology
sections.content:
Product language and terminology

We need consistent, customer-friendly wording:

- **Quantization profile**: A versioned, Redwood-validated configuration for running a specific model variant using a specific quantization method/precision combination.
- **Profile library**: The set of published profiles per model variant. Customers choose a profile for a route.
- **Route-level enablement**: Profiles are enabled per route, not globally for all tenant traffic (v1).
- **Fallback**: If a request is incompatible (hardware/sequence length constraints) or profile application fails safe checks, Redwood serves using baseline precision for that request (or route) while emitting an event.

Avoid ambiguous language:

- Avoid saying “Redwood automatically picks the best profile.”
- Avoid “lossless” claims. Use “aims to preserve quality” and emphasize eval/monitoring.

sections.section_path: Metering To Invoice Reconciliation Playbook > Step-by-step reconciliation procedure > Step 8 — Decide remediation path (forward fix vs adjustment)
sections.heading: Metering To Invoice Reconciliation Playbook > Step-by-step reconciliation procedure > Step 8 — Decide remediation path (forward fix vs adjustment)
sections.content:
Step 8 — Decide remediation path (forward fix vs adjustment)

Use this decision tree once root cause is identified.

**Default policy:** prefer **forward fixes** with clear documentation and audit trail. Avoid retroactive invoice changes.

Remediation options:
1) **No action** (variance within threshold; document)
2) **Forward fix only** (metering bug fixed; applies to future usage)
3) **Customer credit** (invoice remains; credit memo or usage credit issued)
4) **Invoice adjustment / re-issue** (rare; requires CFO + Legal)
5) **Backfill** (usage events/customer export corrected; ledger may or may not change depending on freeze)

Minimum documentation for any remediation:

- Root cause summary
- Impacted period + accounts
- Quantified $ impact (best estimate + bounds)
- Customer comms plan (Support/Sales owner)
- Approvals captured (names + date)

sections.section_path: Hosted Api Slos Enterprise Route Tiers > SLIs (what we measure) > 1) Availability SLI (server success)
sections.heading: Hosted Api Slos Enterprise Route Tiers > SLIs (what we measure) > 1) Availability SLI (server success)
sections.content:
1) Availability SLI (server success)

**Definition:** percentage of requests that return an eligible success response.

- Success codes: `2xx` (and `3xx` if any internal redirects apply; typically none)
- Failures: `5xx`, `408`, `499` (client disconnect) are counted as failures unless explicitly excluded by route-specific rules below.

**Tier handling of 429:**

- **Enterprise:** `429` due to *overload shedding/admission control* counts as **unavailable** (because enterprise is protected; overload shed should be rare and indicates under-provisioning or misconfiguration).
- **Best-effort:** `429` due to overload shedding/admission control does **not** count as unavailable (it is expected behavior under pressure). Quota/rate-limit 429s are not counted as availability failures for either tier.

**Note:** 429 classification must be based on the reason code emitted by gateway/policy engine, not inferred from rate.

[13:22] Chris Osei: Yeah. Proposed test checklist:

2) Verify entitlement exists (via API/console)

4) Generate an API key

[14:03] Miguel Alvarez: That’s good. On cancellation: define your policy. Some partners cut off immediately, some allow a grace period. But it needs to match your listing terms and how you interpret the entitlement state.

[14:18] Cole Summers: Our default is to stop accepting billable traffic if entitlement is inactive, but we may allow a short grace if the cancellation is accidental. For marketplace we probably keep it strict.

[14:31] Anika Desai: During review, they’ll test cancel and see if your UI reflects it. If there’s a grace, document it.

[14:40] Nadia Rahman: On entitlement state changes, how quickly do we see “active -> cancelled”? That’s a potential race.

[14:49] Anika Desai: It’s usually quick, but again, you should poll or have a scheduled sync. Don’t assume immediate.

[15:00] Ben Carter: We have a sync job that runs every few minutes and on-demand verification. We can tighten it during onboarding.

[15:08] Miguel Alvarez: Just be careful with rate limits. If you have everyone spamming “verify entitlement” you might hit quotas. But for normal scale it’s okay.

[15:19] Stephanie Nguyen: One more thing: our SKUs include compliance add-ons (like extended audit log retention, compliance pack). Is it common to have add-ons as separate dimensions or separate plans?

[15:34] Priya Shah: It depends. If it’s truly an add-on, separate plan can be complicated. Some do “bundle plans” (base + add-on). Others handle add-ons off-marketplace. If you want it procured via marketplace, bundling plans is usually easiest.

[15:54] Miguel Alvarez: If you do it as a usage dimension, that’s weird for a monthly compliance pack. Better as subscription line item. But you can create a plan called “Hosted + Compliance” and so on.
